# Closed axes — read this before proposing an experiment

Every row is an axis that has been **measured and closed**. The purpose is not  
bookkeeping: four times now an axis has been re-derived and proposed again — three  
from totals, most recently a monotone transform of the metric term, which  
`fse26-metric-competition-verdict.md` had already excluded by name after building  
and measuring both surviving shapes.

The fourth is the one to learn from, because it was re-derived from a _statistic the  
register itself supplied_: the metric-family gate was proposed again off a  
"flippable vs would-be-hurt" count, which appears in  
`fse26-metric-competition-verdict.md` as a **necessary** condition — and that is  
exactly what it is, not an estimate. Recounted on the shipped configuration it reads  
**79 flippable against 7 hurt** for the connection-pool family, its best ratio ever,  
and the measurement it was proposing had already been run: **+0.14pp with five  
regressed fault types**, and the block it targeted did not move at all. A count of  
cases a change _could_ affect carries no information about the cases it _does_.

## The number that frames every row below

Of the **666 misses** at the shipped configuration (**672** is the same dump's pool-off  
count — the two differ by the six cases the pool penalty fixes, see  
`fse26-shipped-config-verdict.md` §4), **74 (11.1%)** have the winner strictly ahead on  
the metric, the log AND the latency — no non-negative reweighting can put the source  
first, so those need new EVIDENCE. The other **592 (88.9%)** have the source at least  
level with the winner on some term, so each is individually reachable by reweighting.  
The two computations agree exactly: the 74 are precisely the cases labelled  
`metric+log+lat` (73) plus `metric+log+lat+pool` (1), and nothing else is blocked.

Read together with the `logWeight` row — where NO single weight satisfies every case, and  
the per-type oracle ceiling is 50.00% — this locates the obstacle precisely. It is **not**  
absent evidence for 89% of the misses, and it is not a single bad weight: it is **conflict  
between cases**, i.e. demands for opposite weightings from cases that a global (or  
per-fault-type) weight cannot serve at once.

So the lever that is left is a **per-case discriminator** that decides _which term to  
trust_ — a context feature, finer than the fault type. What the existing evidence surfaces  
can supply for that has been measured down: the error text cannot supply direction (19,522  
`ERR:` lines name zero peer services or URLs), per-edge failure counts do not separate  
source from victim at any weight, breadth does not (`latEdges`), the call graph's ancestry  
does not (the source carries a latency rise at all in only 9.3% of the latency-involved  
misses), and every metric-family/label/spacing gate has been measured. **A candidate here  
must name the context feature and show it separates, on a free read, before any run.**

That requirement now has an instrument, and its answer is sharper than the sentence above:  
the PAIRED census (`fse26-separator-verdict.md`) confirms the marginal claims (`failedEdge`  
0.457, `inLatEdges` 0.487, the source's own deviation 0.270 — all pointing at the winner) and  
refines the ancestry one — **the graph's direction separates per population and reverses  
between them**: source → winner in 49 of 65 decisive replace-code pairs (AUC 0.732, stable in  
all 5 folds) against winner → source in 8-32 for network partition and 0-19 for network loss.  
A global graph bonus cannot exist, which is why `failedEdgeWeight = 0` was already closed with  
2 regressed types.

**A proposal must say which rows it does not touch, and why it is not one of  
them.** If it cannot, the first thing to do is read that row's document. If it is  
resting on a necessary-condition count, the second thing is to look for the row that  
measured the change — the count cannot tell you whether it was ever run.

**And a row is found by the KNOB's name, so a search has to know all three of them.**  
A ranking knob is reachable as a `workflow_dispatch` input (`fleet_baseline`), as a  
CLI flag (`--fleet-baseline`) and as an engine option (`metricFleetBaseline`), and only the  
first two are related by a rule. The documents and this register's rows are written in the  
third — so a search for the input name reports four measured-and-rejected knobs as  
unmeasured, which happened here and produced a drafted candidate before an instrument  
caught it. `docs/dispatch-surface-audit.md` is the table that closes it: every ranking knob,  
its three names and its owner, with `packages/kinetic/__tests__/unit/dispatch-surface-census.test.ts`  
requiring that owner to exist, that the four non-derivable names stay an exact set, and that  
the flag a workflow passes is one its runner accepts.

A fifth axis was missing from this table altogether, and it is the first whose record  
lived outside this repo: the LLM-dependent ranking layer — the single-shot  
evidence-grounded reranker and the GALA+ Phase-III multi-hop agent — was measured,  
refuted and **REMOVED** (`0d6ae609`, 19 files, both ablation flags), and a fortnight  
later it was proposed again as the next step, from a note that had never been updated.  
Its row is below, and a test now keeps the retired slice's own symbols out of the tree  
(`packages/kinetic/__tests__/unit/closed-axes-register.test.ts`), because a row is  
prose while this closure was code — and that test failed on its own name list the  
first time it ran, which is why it excludes itself.

The **shipped FSE'26 headline is Top@1 56.12% (798/1422)**, Top@3 69.5%, Top@5 72.0% —  
four measured changes, each on its own runs: the per-edge latency term at  
`latWeight=0.561495` with `latMinRise=10.3` measured together (`34921980498`), the  
pool-dominance penalty at `poolMetricPenaltyWeight=0.0679` measured against its own  
ablation on one commit (`34949812666` / `34949854236`), the stability term at  
`DEFAULT_STABILITY_WEIGHT=0.007352` (`35416576350`, the DEFAULT path with no input  
passed, against the same-commit control `35416580279` at 756 — one case,  
`HTTPResponseReplaceCode 160 → 161`, nothing moving the other way), and the GATED  
failed-edge direction term at `DEFAULT_FAILED_EDGE_WEIGHT=3` (`40072799488` against the  
same-configuration control `35416576350` — **757 → 798, +41 cases, zero regressed fault  
types**, every case of the gain in the network class plus `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod`). **The headline this  
paragraph carried until iteration 29 — 53.16% (756/1422), Top@3 66.46%, Top@5 70.25% —  
is the SAME configuration one enrolment earlier**, reachable as `stability_weight=0`;  
its row is 750 lines below, where the enrolment was recorded while this one kept the  
number a reader meets FIRST. That is the register's own named failure mode — **a  
summary outlives its own correction** — committed in the register's own opening, which  
is why the four changes are now listed with their runs rather than summarised by the  
latest of them. The 52.74% (750/1422) with Top@3 65.75% and Top@5 70.11% is the same  
configuration with the pool penalty off as well — reachable as  
`--pool-penalty 0`. Verdicts written earlier quote a **47.33%** or  
**48.80%** control: those rows are historical records of what their ablation was  
measured against, not the current number. Both are still reachable as ablations — the  
`latWeight=0` control, and the `latMinRise=1` credited-everything shape at 48.80%.

| the log term's **SCALE** — `logNormalisation` = `max` / `saturating` (κ) / `share` — i.e. the divisor that turns an admitted COUNT into a score                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `log-volume-scale.md`, `benchmarks/src/log-flood-census.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **FIVE ARMS, ALL REJECTED, AND THE AXIS CLOSED AS A FAMILY RATHER THAN AS A KNOB.** Shipped `max` = **484/711 (68.07%)**; `saturating` κ=100 → 460 (−24), κ=25 → 450 (−34), κ=10 → 437 (−47), κ=5 → 437 (−47); `share` → **474 (−10)**, the best departure; `logWeight=0` → 362 (−122), which is the control that prices the term at all. The five are not five guesses: they are the only three things a per-case divisor can be (the case's maximum, a constant, the case's total), and together they separate the two properties a divisor carries — **magnitude** and **ratio**. The separation is exact: `saturating` κ=25 claims a mean champion weight of **0.622** and scores 450, `share` claims **0.609** and scores **474** — same magnitude, 24 cases apart — so the loss was never about how much weight the term claims, it is the RATIO compression, which is why the least-curved divisor is the best of the four. What survives every member is the register's conflict, sharper than before: with ratios preserved exactly, the replacement population still wants MORE log weight (205 cases, −13) and the delay population still wants LESS (119 cases, +6), and the lifecycle families are byte-identical in all six arms because their sources are log-silent. The census says why no schedule can exist — the oracle weight is **bimodal**: the truth is the top emitter in 38.1% of cases (ideal weight ≥ 1) and emits NOTHING under a neighbour's flood in 16.9% (ideal weight exactly 0), with 34.5% of the corpus admitting at most one line and 15.8% tying at the top so `max` pays `1.0` to several services at once. The only observable proposed for that split — emitter concentration — was already refuted as a HARD gate (`logicHttpDominant`, 5 regressed types, one non-regressing threshold at +1); `share` is the continuous version of that same statistic and it loses too, which is the second independent refutation and the reason this row closes the family. The second mechanism hides behind the first: even the mutual graph reports `0`, because the BFS reads intensity on the **last** step and the explicit Euler update overshoots at `n → 1`, `n + di·dt` goes negative, and `Math.max(0, …)` pins it there — measured `max 1.0, final 0`. Measured A/B (coupling 0.9, τ = 60 s, 300 s horizon): `a→b→c` peak **0.000 → 0.293**, distance **0 → 2**; `a→b→c→d→e` **0.000 → 0.135**, distance **0 → 4**; the mutual pair keeps peak 1.000 but its published series no longer ends pinned at exactly 0. `cascade-model.ts` moves from 99.21/93.93 to **100/100/100/100**. **RCAEval numbers are unaffected**: `cascadeResult` is attached to `rca-pipeline`’s return value, no ranking term reads it, and `enableWave` gates the stage. | the **PAIRED** separator question — which dump-visible signal prefers the true source to the engine's rank-1, per fault type — for all 14 declared signals                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `fse26-separator-verdict.md`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | 666 pairs, 250 non-term cells, bar `Sidak(0.05, 250) = p < 2.05e-4`: **no signal separates globally** (the best non-term signal is `onset` at AUC 0.537, under the 0.60 criterion); **4/250 separate FOR the source** and **35/250 AGAINST it**, six of those deterministic (`JVMMemoryStress/transientDrops` 0-159, `kept` 0-158, `sigLines` 0-105; `ContainerKill/kept` 0-83, `transientDrops` 1-82; `JVMMemoryStress/reaches` 11-110). Only two of the four hold in **every fold**: `NetworkPartition/errLines` 30-3 (AUC 0.781, p=1.4e-6) and `HTTPResponseReplaceCode/reaches` 49-16 (AUC 0.732, p=5.1e-5); `JVMMemoryStress/inDegree` (98-48) and `NetworkLoss/inDegree` (21-2) each have a fold at exactly 0.500. 43/666 pairs carry NO non-term preference for the source at all — **over ten signals**; the field audit (`SERVICE_FIELD_AUDIT`, typed `Record<keyof DiagnosedService, string>` so a new reader field cannot reach main unclassified) then named the fields that were read but not screened, five more signals were added, and the re-run over **375 non-term cells** reports **13/375 for the source and 37/375 against** it. Two findings, one of which survives: the raw `failedEdge` COUNT separates at **0.908** on replace-code (60-2, stable in all five folds) where the gated SCORE does not (0.457) — the register's "per-edge counts do not separate" is true of the score and false of the count — while the four `decisive*` composition signals (leader `decisiveCv` AUC 0.734, p=2.0e-40) are **NOT established**: the conditioning that would separate them from the renderer's brevity has 0-5 pairs to stand on in every block type, i.e. the confound is saturated instead of excluded. **The reader feeding them was itself wrong, and is now fixed and re-measured.** `inventoryOf` selected the decomposition by largest `riseRatio`, on the claim that "the metric that drove the score is the one with the largest rise" — which the engine's own `dominant` name contradicts in **751 of the 7,733 decomposed rows (9.7%)**: the decisive metric IS the score argmax, the rendered list is sorted by score, so the name was already in the dump to be read. Reading the named metric (fallback: the highest-scoring entry; never the rise) moves every aggregate one way — `decisiveCv` 0.734 → **0.738** (p 2.0e-40 → 7.9e-42, losses 132 → 129) — all of it on the **shipped** dump `r35006947938`, whose header carries `latWeight=0.561495 latMinRise=10.3 poolMetricPenaltyWeight=0.0679` and NO temporal override, and which yields the **666** pairs this row was written from. **Provenance note, because the first attempt got it wrong**: the same measurement on `r35029055764` gave 662 pairs and was labelled "shipped" in two documents; that dump's header pins `temporalWeight=0.036552 onsetShape=earliest-only`, i.e. the REJECTED onset pair, and the register's own 0.734/2.0e-40 turning up as that dump's pre-fix value is what confirmed it. Read the header, never the filename, `decisiveBaseline` 0.628 → **0.644**, `decisiveBurst` 0.571 → 0.577, `JVMMemoryStress/decisiveCv` 0.682 → 0.689, `HTTPResponseReplaceCode/decisiveCv` 59-3 → 58-3, and `PodFailure/decisiveCv` **0.958 → 1.000 (24-0, stable in all five folds)** — and the UNCONDITIONAL rate does not reopen it, for a reason that is now a number: `kept` and `decisiveCv` correlate at **r = 0.4325 (ρ = 0.4086)** across the pairs' 1,332 services, and the source keeps FEWER metrics than the winner in **514 of 666** pairs (more in 126, equal in 26). **The matched comparison does reopen it, and it is now an instrument rather than a paragraph**: `INVENTORY_MATCH_BAND = 2` with `inventoryComparable`, a `kept<=` column on every row and a `near` sub-cell on every cell, whose legend states that the matched stratum is NOT the whole population. On the same dump the confound stops being a separator under matching (`kept` 0.209 → **0.271**) while `decisiveCv` retains **0.718 on 487 pairs** — the ONLY non-term rate that clears the 0.6 criterion on that stratum (`decisiveBaseline` 0.598 is next and falls short). Per type, matched: `ReplaceCode/decisiveCv` **0.885** (48), `PodFailure/decisiveCv` **1.000** (23), `JVMMemoryStress/decisiveCv` 0.661 (87), `ContainerKill/decisiveCv` 0.637 (40), `ReplaceCode/edgeRecords` 0.865 (48), `NetworkPartition/errLines` 0.793 (46). Quote **0.718**, not 0.738: the unconditional rate is an upper bound under a confound that is measured rather than assumed | a candidate built on `edgeRecords`, screened on a **different** held-out fifth and fitted per POPULATION (the network types reverse it) — and, for the `decisive*` family, **instrumentation** — specifically an **inventory-MATCHED** comparison: exact-`kept` matches are 26 of 662, so the confound check needs a coarsened match at a stated band before it has any power. a **candidate run** for `decisiveCv` — the window solver on both benchmarks, fitted per population, with the standing rule that a paired preference is not a term (`fse26-term-oracle-verdict.md` §9). **The solver this names now exists and the FSE'26 half is SOLVED**, behind `--cv-screen` (`fse26-cv-screen.md`): on all 1422 cases of run `35107871516` the `rank` shape has a zero-regression window at `[0.029860, 0.030480]` — gain 6, `lostAtShip` 0, `ship 0.030170`, Top@1 756→**762 (+0.42pp)**, the same 6-case magnitude the shipped pool penalty was accepted on — and `flip` gains 3. The instrument's self-check is exact (`correct at 0` 756 = the run's published 53.16%), and both the per-case closed forms and a direct re-ranking at five weights reproduce it. What is owed is therefore only the **golden half**, which cannot be measured offline because the term is not in the engine: an opt-in fusion weight defaults to 0, so enrolling it leaves the golden configuration bit-for-bit unchanged and the candidate is measured by PASSING THE FLAG, not by moving the default. The inventory match is no longer the blocker: what a run has to respect is the matched stratum (487 of 666, and the 179 dropped are the pairs whose inventories differ most) and the family split (`decisiveTrend` 0.372 the other way). Rendering the decisive metric for every service was never the missing instrument — the asymmetry is in how many metrics each side KEEPS. **The candidate run the condition asked for has now been taken**: `35125277962` at `stabilityWeight=0.03017` against the control `35125285784` on the same commit (`95f963c`), where the control reproduces the shipped headline exactly — **756 / 53.2%**, Top@3 66.5%, Top@5 70.3% — and the candidate delivers **+5 cases and 0 regressed fault types**: 761 / 53.5%, Top@3 66.7%, Top@5 70.5%, with `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` 160→161, `JVMMemoryStress` 12→13, `HTTPResponseDelay` 52→53, `HTTPResponseReplaceBody` 45→46, `JVMException` 30→31 and no type down. The solver claimed **6**; the case it did not collect is the one its own margin list names as thinnest — **1.054e-4** at the shipped weight, against `3.129e-4` for the next and a rank step of **6.034e-4** — a step the SHAPE's own law supplies, and the screen now names which: the same artifact's `flip` row reads **3.086e-5** (a printed-digit step, `quantum/scale`, 15× smaller at the same shipped weight, and it moves `10.2×` with one more digit where the rank step does not move at all — the same asymmetry the span carries, because a sub-quantum difference becomes a whole RANK STEP for one shape and only the quantum itself for the other) — and the dump renders every input at three decimals, so the sixth gain was never resolvable from it. That margin is a scale and not a calibrated threshold (`3.129e-4` is also under `1e-3` and that case WAS collected); what it buys is that `--cv-screen` now prints it, so a knife-edge claim is visible before a run rather than only after one. What is still owed is the **golden half**: at the enrolling commit `0ab737f` the run `35125060855` reproduces **all nine cells** (`RE1 80 / 92.8 / 68`, `RE2 82.4 / 88.9 / 68.1`, `RE3 80 / 45 / 51.1`) — which is the DEFAULT path, where the weight is 0, so it is the enrolment that is verified rather than the weight. The weight's own golden is unmeasured and cannot be argued away (the field exists on RCAEval too), so the term SHIPS at 0.007352: 0.030170 was the WINDOW's own midpoint and it is a REJECTED point, while 0.007352 is the midpoint of the INTERSECTION and both halves were measured green; `earliest-only` passed this same FSE'26 half completely and then moved six of nine cells by up to 41pp. **That half has now been measured, and it is a VETO.** `run-rcaeval.ts` gained `--stability-weight` (default read from the engine's `DEFAULT_STABILITY_WEIGHT`, so a push-triggered run is byte-identical) and `benchmark-rcaeval.yml` the matching `workflow_dispatch` input, and the dispatched run `35132525118` at `5233678` with `stability_weight=0.03017` **moves four of nine cells**: `RE1 OnlineBoutique 80.0 → 79.2`, `RE1 TrainTicket 68.0 → 67.2`, **`RE2 TrainTicket 68.1 → 52.3` (−15.8pp)**, `RE3 SockShop 45.0 → 47.5`. So 0.03017 buys +5 on FSE'26 and costs four golden cells, one of them by 15.8pp: under the shared kill criterion the WEIGHT is rejected and its default stays 0. Two things are now measurable that were not: the resolution of the count itself (`gainResolution`, in `fse26-cv-screen.md` §4 — at 0.030170 the `rank` shape's six gains hold in 22.5% of 400 seeded resamplings of the digits the producer discards, **five in 36.0%**, four in 30.5%, three in 8.8%, two in 2.3%, and **1 of 6** holds in every one, so the run's own five is the MODAL outcome while `flip`'s three hold 95.3% of the time), and the second benchmark at any weight via the flag. **The second benchmark can now be solved OFFLINE as well**: `run-rcaeval.ts` emits the same diagnostic dump the FSE'26 runner does (`--diagnose-dump`, driven by `benchmark-rcaeval.yml`'s `diagnose_dump` input, one file per invocation and shipped as an artifact), assembled by the ONE writer `buildFSE26Diagnostic` — which is what found the second defect: that runner derived the failed-edge record count and the inbound latency rise from the raw converter's tuples while the loaded case already carried the loader's normalised form of both, i.e. two sources for one number, and the reason no second runner could reuse the builder. So one dispatch now buys every subsequent weight: the window solver, the family screen and the decisive-stability screen run on the golden's own case set at no further cost, and the reopening condition is checkable before the money is spent rather than after. **The first dispatch has now been read, and it described less of its run than it appeared to, twice.** `--suite re1` evaluates 375 cases (125 in each of three systems) and the artifact held **125 blocks, every one of them tagged `re1tt`**: the runner built the text per group and called `writeFileSync` INSIDE the group loop, so each system truncated the last one's while the console printed the same `125 cases, 125 blocks` three times. And `Config:` appears **0 times in all seven dumps** against the FSE'26 dump, which opens with the run's own line — so the `re3` dump, the only one dispatched with `traceWeight=1`, reconstructs to `correct at 0 1` against its own `prediction= 15` with nothing in the file to explain it. Both are fixed by one owner for the file (`DiagnoseDump`): records accumulate across every group, `write()` runs once after the last group, a record after the write and a second write both RAISE, and the file opens with `formatSignalLine(opts)` — the banner's own string, so artifact and console cannot state different modes. Measured on a three-system fixture with the same input: **old 3 blocks, all `re1tt`, no header; new 9 blocks, `re1ob 3 / re1ss 3 / re1tt 3`, header = the banner line**. The fidelity question is now answered as a table rather than an assurance: against each dump's OWN `prediction=` rank the reconstruction is **exact on all four `traceWeight=0` dumps** (`re1` 85, `re1-noinject` 85, `re2` 33, and even `re3-noinject`'s 1 of 30) and diverges **only** on the trace-augmented one (15 → 1), which is the one term the reconstruction does not model — so a `traceWeight=0` dump is screenable, a `traceWeight>0` dump is not, and the instrument says which it is holding. **And then the base every screen reconstructs on was found to be gap-wrong.** A paired dispatch at `stability_weight=0.030170` WITH `diagnose_dump` (`35181249060`) makes the dump's own `prediction=` list the engine's ranking at that weight, so the engine's flips are readable case by case: **re1 gained 1 / lost 3, re2 gained 0 / lost 8, re3-noinject gained 1 / lost 0**. Against the screen's own version of that term — its `rank` shape, which IS the engine's `computeStabilityScores` — the screen reads **300 (1/2), 111 (0/8, every NAME identical), 37 (0/0)**: exact on `re2`, and two cases out on the other two suites. The `+7 / −13` quoted before that was the screen's DEFAULT (`flip`) shape measured against a rank-shaped engine term — two different quantities. The cause is a wrong QUANTITY in `blendScores` plus a CONDITION it did not carry: the engine takes `log1p` of the node's anomaly AS THE TOPOLOGY BUILDER LEFT IT (`pruner.ts` 1400/1575), and that builder rescales the vector only at or above `ANOMALY_NORMALIZE_NODE_THRESHOLD` nodes (`topology-fault-graph.ts` step 1b; 20, now an exported owner), while the reconstructor substituted a re-derived rank rescale unconditionally (`fse26-term-oracle.ts` 219, deleted). The rescale is monotone, so the ORDER was the engine's on every case and the GAPS were not on any case below the threshold: **407 of the golden's 615 cases** (`re1` 250/375, `re2` 100/150, `re3` 57/90 — the OB and SS systems at 12–19 services) and **0 of FSE'26's 1422**, where every case is 51 or 52 services (`{51: 1417, 52: 5}` measured on the dump) — which is exactly why only the second benchmark could expose it, and why the FSE'26 headline is untouched. The fidelity line could not have exposed it either, and for a worse reason: it printed a metric-term deviation of `2.51e+0` over `3500` of its `11557` services on `re1` — a deviation with no unit, no population and no pass condition, read as a rounding detail for as long as the defect lived. **Corrected and re-measured**: the metric term is read off the row (`log1p(service.selfAnomaly)`), `metricSlopes` is deleted rather than documented, the threshold is exported with a test that pins BOTH sides on a real graph (19 nodes raw vs 20 rescaled, and the flag provably inert below it), the producer's `selfAnomaly` contract no longer claims "[0, 1] rank-normalised" (false on two thirds of the golden), and the deviation counter is replaced by the population split plus the check that CAN fail — at or above the threshold no value may EXCEED 1, measured **0 cases** on every dump read, and reported separately from the 34 of 1422 FSE'26 cases whose maximum is BELOW 1.000 because a TIED top anomaly takes its tie group's mean rank (`47.5 / 50` for a six-way tie — the first counter written claimed a 1.000 maximum instead and the first real dump falsified it, which is why the falsifiable half and the population fact are now two lines). The regression proof is that every fidelity number is bit-identical (`correct at 0` 301/301/119/119/35/37/37, and `rank-1 same as the dump's own recorded` 375/375 · 375/375 · 150/150 · 150/150 · 70/90 · 90/90 · 90/90) and the whole FSE'26 half is byte-identical (`correct at 0` 756, `rank` gain 6 at `[0.029860, 0.030480]` ship `0.030170`, `flip` gain 3 at `[0.021536, 0.024882]` ship `0.023209`, both margins, both resolution lines). What moved is the golden's own window arithmetic: `re1` `flip` ship `0.007968 → 0.008032`, `rank` cap `0.015112 → 0.015233`, and at the weight `flip` `295 → 294` with gained `7 → 6` (`re2` and `re3-noinject` unchanged at `107`/`37`), plus the FSE'26 resolution histogram — with a stated cause: `gainResolution` resamples the render's discarded digits, and the old base RE-RANKED a resampled row, so its jitter moved the term by a rank step (≈`1/50`) instead of a digit. At `0.030170` the six gains now hold in 23.5% of the 400 seeded draws and **2 of 6 in every draw**, against the old 22.5% and 1 of 6. The two residuals are NAMED rather than inferred, and both decide on a pair whose `cv` renders equal (`0.050` vs `0.050`; `0.045` vs `0.045`) while the engine ranks on the unrounded field — so no weight can reorder them from this artifact, and "unreachable at every weight" now has a third cause besides "no decisive composition" and "the term cannot cross the gap". So: the VETO stands (it is a run's own measurement), the term stays admitted at 0.03017 and off by default, every window figure in `fse26-cv-screen.md` is quoted against the corrected base, and the correction's own golden is **9 of 9 cells byte-identical** (`35199445631` at `8bcf16c`: `RE1 80.0 / 92.8 / 68.0`, `RE2 82.4 / 88.9 / 68.1`, `RE3 80.0 / 45.0 / 51.1`, every job green) — the kill criterion's second half, measured by the push that carried the change rather than asserted. **And the unreachable count now travels with its causes**, because one count read the same whether the term had no input here, read a deciding pair as EQUAL, or genuinely could not reach: FSE'26 `rank` **526 = 0 root-without-a-row + 0 no spread + 0 unweighed + 226 tied at the render + 300 out of reach** (`flip` 569 = 0 + 0 + 0 + 236 + 333), `re1` `rank` 52 = 0 + 0 + 0 + 20 + 32, `re2` 24 = 0 + 0 + 0 + 11 + 13, `re3-noinject` 37 = 0 + 0 + 0 + 25 + 12 — five classes, because an equal slope the term weighed on NEITHER side is a pair the ENGINE cannot separate either, and it reads 0 on every dump here — with every total IDENTICAL before and after the split (measured on the same dumps) so the classes are a refinement of the count rather than a new one. That is how one of the two residual disagreements — `re3ss_front-end_f3_2`, whose deciding pair renders `cv=0.045` twice — became a CLASS rather than something a hand-diff against the engine had to find; the other, `re1ob_currencyservice_delay_4`, is on the CAP side, and the mirror class is now built and NAMES it: **the cap is an UPPER bound** — 31 of `re1`'s 301 satisfied cases, 14 of `re2`'s 119 and 510 of FSE'26's 756 hold a rival the artifact cannot order (on FSE'26 the cap's own case is one of them), each case's frontier being a gap the engine ranks on the unrounded `cv`. **The count is a count of a BOX and not of a benchmark**: the class is _pairs the RENDER cannot tell apart_, so a finer render splits them — FSE'26's own class is **356 of 756 at four decimals**, a 30% shrink on the same 1422 cases, and every count in this paragraph is quoted at the three decimals those dumps declare. The class is a NECESSARY condition and the paired dispatch confirms it in the only direction that can be checked: **exactly one satisfied-side disagreement exists (`re1ob_currencyservice_delay_4`) and it is inside the class**, while the engine's other losses at that weight (2 of 3 on `re1`, all 8 on `re2`) are ones the model predicts too. **And the class carries its own bound rather than a caveat**: an equal rendered `cv` means the two services sit in ONE rounding cell, so the engine's slope gap for the pair cannot exceed what THAT SHAPE's spacing can hide — `(g − 1)/(n − 1)` for a shape that re-ranks, `quantum/(scale − quantum)` for one that is LINEAR in the value — and the earliest weight it can cost the case is `lead / span`. Over the class that is `lossFloor`, **0.003873 on FSE'26 against a cap of 0.030480 (8× under it)** on the `rank` shape, 0.008032 against 0.015233 on `re1`'s `rank` shape, and above the cap on `re2` where the channel cannot bind at all. **The two laws are not interchangeable, and the gap between them is the shape's own exposure to the render's resolution**: on FSE'26 the same class and the same leads give `rank` `0.003873` and `flip` `1.457280` at four decimals — a sub-quantum difference becomes a whole RANK STEP for a shape that re-ranks and only the quantum itself for one that is linear, so a finer render leaves the rank-spaced exposure bounded away from zero (`0.1%` across one digit) while the value-linear one VANISHES (`10.1×`) — and the class's own count shrinks with the quantum for the same reason. What is NOT a property of the shape is the class's MEMBERSHIP: both shapes are strictly monotone in `cv`, so two services one cell cannot tell apart are one cell apart under either. The floor is a PERMISSION and not a prediction, and the one run that measured it says so: the FSE'26 candidate delivered +5 cases with **0 regressed fault types** at 0.030170, so the engine's own cap is above that weight and the bound is loose by more than 8× there. **And the separator's own instrument has since caught a THIRD defect in itself, whose reach is the census's Finding 7**: `bestDev` and `bestRise` were maxima initialised at `0`, so a service whose block rendered an inventory and NO decomposition read `0` — the value a decomposed zero-deviation metric also takes. `SeparatorScalar.of` already reserves `undefined` for "an inventory the block did not render" and the container `rendered` already honours it; the rule had been applied to the container and not to the two numbers inside it, and a test on exactly that fixture asserted it for the three `decisive*` signals while `bestDev`/`bestRise` on the same fixture returned `0`. Measured in production on `artifacts/diag-34684319273` (2095 inventories, **zero** decompositions, 2094 labelled rows): **319 pairs decided as ties at 0.500 with the `n/a` column at zero → 319 `unmeasurable`**, and a full-report diff over six artifacts shows `re3`, `artifacts/r34919714864` and **the shipped dump this row's table is read from** bit-identical (`bestRise / bestDev` 0.270, `180–486–0`, unchanged), `re1`/`re2` one pair each into `n/a` (`bestDev` 74→73, 31→30) (`docs/fse26-separator-verdict.md` §2.3) |

| `drop-deviation-symmetry.md` | **the axis #193 closed, reopened where its precondition now exists, as a PAIR.** `deviation = log₁₀(1 + max(rise, drop))` is unbounded in the rise direction and capped at `log₁₀2 ≈ 0.301` for a drop — so `ts-route-service`'s `socket` 18 → 11 (dev 0.356) can never out-score a victim's latency rise (dev 1.7), which is the blocking cell's signature in every failure block, and PRISM's `|mean shift|` has no such asymmetry. `log` measures a drop against its POST-drop level so a 10× drop reads what a 10× rise reads, while being IDENTICAL for rises (`post/base = 1 + riseRatio`) — so it is an axis about drops, not a re-scoring. It is only readable NOW because two guards arrived after #193: the event/idle guard (`min < max × 0.001`) removes the collapse-to-zero that exploded, and `metricRiseCeiling` bounds the ratio itself — which is why the arm set includes `dropdev=log` ALONE (the reproduction of the refusal), `ceil=10` alone, and the pair. **MEASURED, ALL THREE REFUSED**: `log` alone **480/735 (−126)** and FSE'26 Top@1 **51.5% (−4.9 pp)** — the #193 explosion quantified, worst on RE2 (231 → 156) where a collapsing resource metric is the victim's signature; `log + ceil=10` **576**, i.e. the ceiling recovers **96 of the 126** and leaves a −30 residue that is a real loss; `ceil=10` alone **600** with **RE3 52 → 56** (all four in SockShop) at RE1 **−7** — the best arm of the iteration and still below the price of a four-case lead. The measured exchange rate is the section's finding: every lever that raises RE3 lowers RE1 (PRISM conjunctive +9/−37, mask 0/−33, ceiling +4/−7) except the burst removal (+2/+4), so only a lever ORTHOGONAL to the rise/drop direction has ever moved both. `bounded` ships and is bit-identical to the old expression by construction (`max` of two monotone logs = log of the max ratio), and `metricRiseCeiling` had been FSE'26-only, so the golden half could not state the value every published number ran at — forwarded here on both halves, which retires its exemption in `UNREPORTED_BY_ENGINE_RUNNERS` |

The thresholds are imported from `DEFAULT_TRACE_ACTIVITY_OPTIONS`, so the label cannot name a guard the rule stopped using. **READ, and it refutes the prediction written before the run**: on TrainTicket `truth-pre<500=0` — not one wrong vote was excluded by the volume floor — while `truth-rise<1.15=5` of 5, and the truth's count FELL on every one of them (`growth` 0.82 / 0.91 / 0.92 / 0.93 / 0.94 on `pre ≈ 12 000`, i.e. 700–2 200 spans the fault removed), against fifteen hits that are all ONE service at `pre ≈ 1.8 k`, `growth` 1.17–2.22. `truth-qualified=0` on both voting cells, so the census and the rule still agree about what the rule accepts. **The premise "a source does MORE work per request" is false on exactly the cases the term misses** — this is the `trace (source ratio < 1)` channel §168 enumerated, now COUNTED: 5 of 5. | whether the trace candidate's rise can be put on a **SCALE-FREE axis** — the four prior refinements were each a refusal about the SHAPE of the evidence (weight, leader mask, tail-only, materiality floor), and the riser census left exactly one shape standing: the hits are ONE small service with large ratios while the misses are LARGE services with modest ones, so a percentage threshold is loud where the counts are small and deaf where they are large | `trace-z.md` | **the axis carries the magnitude and the SELECTOR is refused — the fifth refusal of this family.** `z = (post − r·pre)/√(r·pre)` with `r` the UNWEIGHTED median of the per-service ratios (a volume ratio absorbs the fault's own service into its denominator: 1 000 missing spans on `pre = 12 000` normalise to `z ≈ −1.3` instead of `−9.1`), measured on `40792623427` at `ea47db5`, RE3 only because the corpus gates span counts on `meta.suite === 'RE3'`. **The good news is the largest statement this term has ever had**: on TrainTicket the truth is a ≥ 3σ deviator on **23 of 30** cases and the LOUDEST deviator on **15 of 30** — against the anomaly axis where the same truth is mid-pack 33 of 68 — so the span counts do know where the source is, and what fails is the reading of them. **The refusal is the selectors**: `zAbs` casts ZERO votes on TrainTicket because a fleet-wide collapse (drift 0.05–0.11) makes dozens of services significant at once and uniqueness never holds; `zUp` votes 2 and is right 2, but **surrenders 13 of the engine's 15 hits**; and on OnlineBoutique `zAbs`'s 11 votes include 4 hits that are ALL cases the engine already answers correctly, while the cell's six misses are missed twice over (on the two `cartservice` cases the truth is not in the trace population at all — `truth-measured = 18 of 30` — and on the three `currencyservice` cases three services cross 3σ together). The five route misses' truth is not loud and NEGATIVE as the prediction said: it reads `z = −0.7 / −6.0 / +3.0 / −4.1 / −0.7` at `|z|` ranks 21 / 5 / 18 / 7 / 22, i.e. **below the noise of its own 12 000-span baseline** once the fleet collapses | **CLOSED in five forms**; the ratio rule keeps the cell and the pin keeps its +10 cases. What would reopen it: a corpus where the fault does not collapse the fleet (every RCAEval trace case where the truth rises does collapse it, drift 0.05–0.15), or a direction-carrying signal that can separate a source from its victim, which `trace-riser.md` §6 measured to be `+0` everywhere on this corpus |
| the **SILENCE prior** — whether a service whose disturbance is LOW relative to its own fan-in can be ranked above louder candidates, which is the only form that fits a cell where the truth is the quietest 11 of 14 times | `re3-quiet-truth.md` | **the inversion is MEASURED (11 of 14 quietest, 0 of 14 loudest, twice); the term is NOT built**, because the decisive statistic — the anomaly of EVERY graph member, not just the top-5 — is not on the artifact yet and this month's record is that a term built without its instrument is measured on the wrong quantity | **DONE in iteration 143** — `GT rank=<r> of <n>` on every failure block, which answered the question and CORRECTED the audit's own headline (mid-pack 33 of 68, not quietest). **And the lever it pointed at is ENROLLED in iteration 144**: PRISM's shape test imported as PRESENCE (`dualFamilyWeight = 0.25`, a 0/1 membership rather than a score) takes RE3 **52 → 55** with RE1 and RE2 **BYTE-IDENTICAL** — the first arm this month with no cell down — and is inert on FSE'26 by construction. What stays open is why the membership finds SockShop's truth and not TrainTicket's — and **that question is answered in iteration 145, by a measurement that CORRECTS this row's own premise**: both statistics are the SAME (`computeChannelExtremes` calls PRISM's `deviationZScore`, not the composition's `log₁₀(1 + ratio)`), so nothing could have been separated on that axis. The difference is DENSITY: the census added in `dual-family-gate.md` reads 81.7% of OnlineBoutique RE1's fleet inside the family with the truth inside it 98.4% of the time, and a constant bonus paid to 82% of a cell cannot re-order it |
| the deviation WINDOW's anchor — whether a metric's baseline, `max` and `min` come from the whole file or from the segment before the injection, which is the difference between scoring a fault against the level a service RUNS at and against the level it warmed up to | `baseline-anchor.md` | **built, tested, dispatchable on both halves, and now MEASURED ON ALL NINE CELLS AND BOTH SUITES — and the answer is: the axis works, the default does not move.** Three arms on the 735-case corpus (pre-clause `e79c0b61` 627, control 631, anchored 634) price the two changes APART: the log-vocabulary clause is `+11/−7 = +4` and the window is `+13/−10 = +3`, and **the intersection of the two move-sets is EMPTY**, so the pair is strictly additive (627 + 4 + 3 = 634) — a single arm would have split +7 between two mechanisms by assertion. Per cell the window reads SS1 `116 → 119`, TT3 `21 → 25`, SS3 `18 → 19`, OB2 `80 → 79`, TT2 `75 → 72`, OB3 `25 → 24`. On FSE'26 it is `Top@1 60.478% → 61.181%` (+10 of 1422, `Top@3` +8, `Top@5` +6), and the clause is provably INERT there (`PROPAGATED_EXCEPTION_PATTERN` is reachable from one loader, and the pre-clause run reproduces `0.6047819971870605` to sixteen digits). The mechanism is still counted on `re3ss_carts_f4_2`: the truth's own `cpu` rises 5.8× from the level it runs at (4.41) to the warm-up level (29.99) and the whole-file window scores that as `drop=1.00, dev=0.301`, the capped end of the drop side, against `dev=0.833` anchored. **Ships at `whole-file`, i.e. OFF**: `RE2:TrainTicket 75 → 72` is a cell regression and a cell regression is refused on measurement even when the corpus total improves. The loss concentration bought a SECOND value rather than a default: `pre-injection-stationary` is the same window with one refusal — it anchors only when the pre-segment certifies itself as a level, `DRIFT = |median(second half) − median(first half)| / |median(pre-segment)| ≤ 0.25` over at least 6 samples, both halves summarised by the same MEDIAN the baseline uses. **Measured on all nine cells it is `635/735` (`+5/−4` against the unguarded arm) and it recovers exactly the losses it was built for — both remaining RE2:TrainTicket `_1` cases and the RE3:OnlineBoutique loss — at the price of four of the unguarded arm's near-swaps; on FSE'26 it is `864` against `870`, so the two suites DISAGREE and the condition cannot be stationarity alone.** The statistic already computes a SIGNED difference and the guard throws the sign away: a pre-segment that opens high and settles (this axis' founding case) and one that is still climbing are both `non-stationary` to it, and the next value has to separate them. | **the warm-up prediction is resolved, and half of it is FALSIFIED — which is what the row is for.** It predicted that losses "must fall in the warm-up population (`mem`/`cpu` series that open high)"; the concentration is real but it is on injection **INDEX**, not on family: **5 of the 10 losses are `_1` cases** (all five RE2-TT moves are, four losses and one gain), while the families are `disk`×3, `loss`×2, `delay`, `cpu`, `f*`×3. So the condition that predicts the losses is _the pre-window is the container's own ramp_ — a STATIONARITY condition — and the guard that follows is a stationarity test on the pre-window, not a family mask. Two further gates before the default may move: the run carries **no counter for refused anchors** (short window, non-positive baseline, `max(3, ⌈0.1n⌉)`), so "cell X did not move" cannot yet be told apart from "the guard refused the anchor on every series in X"; and it still does not compose with `dropdev=log`, whose explosion was measured against the whole-file window **The counter now exists** (`benchmarks/src/anchor-census.ts`, 100% covered, called through the engine's own `probePreInjectionWindow`/`judgePreWindowDrift` so the count and the decision cannot disagree), and its first reading closed the sign hypothesis rather than confirming it: a fourth value `pre-injection-non-rising` (refuse only a RISING pre-segment, `drift > 0.25`) was dispatched on all nine cells and FSE'26 and TIES the symmetric guard at `635/735` while losing `870 → 866` on FSE'26 — `stationary → non-rising` is `+4/−4`, four cases bought by refusing a SETTLING segment and four by allowing a RISING one, so no single threshold on one statistic can have both halves. The census also priced the guard's own population for the first time: the rising share of placeable series ranges from `0.6%` (RE2:OnlineBoutique) to `12.6%` (RE3:TrainTicket), a factor of 21, so a global threshold cannot be right at both ends. And it moved the next lever off this axis: the 23 moves of the unguarded arm separate on the CANDIDATE POOL (median 15 for gains, **39** for losses) and not on the truth's pre-window (gains `{level 4, settling 8, rising 1}` vs losses `{level 4, settling 6}`), i.e. the losses are a property of the ranking's DENSITY — `rankNormalization` and the top-of-graph score gap — rather than of the window's admissibility |
| the **expected-outlier RATE as an elimination DECIDER** — whether a candidate whose channels leave their fault-free bands in most clean windows can be demoted in favour of one whose evidence is rarer, stated as a claim over the posterior rather than as a weight on it | `agentic-headroom.md` §5, on 711 converted RCABench cases against a 2 077-channel profile built from the same corpus | most permissive thresholds **46.3 % against the engine's 68.07 %** (−21.8 pp, 310 moves); the best held-out point **68.2 % against 68.75 %** there — four moves and −0.6 pp. The census says why: mean channel rate **0.749**, median 0.796, only **0.8 %** of channels clean, so "left its band" is not rare and a rate that counts it orders nothing| **CLOSED as a decider** — the third presentation to fail (additive term in iteration 265, this rule, and the column that survives only because its job is to make a claim checkable rather than to decide it). The layer keeps the column and the +16.63 pp ceiling it makes checkable |

| **the weight vector as a DIRECTION** — every term moved at once, which no screen here had ever done: 28 single-term points, 84 revival points and a resolution floor are points on the AXES of a 14-dimensional space | `weight-reachability.md` | **REOPENED, and then constrained.** The hull theorem decides every case exactly: with the formula's support frozen, **131 of 349 misses are provably unreachable** by any re-weighting; with the support open, **all 349** are reachable, each by a vector of its own. A single vector fitted on half the corpus and read on the other half gains **+38 to +52 (mean +47.3, +6.7 pp)** in **six of six** fits — so 274's _"not reachable by re-weighting"_ was a statement about the axes it swept. It does not ship YET: the family gate (`n ≥ 20` may not lose a case) rejects it on `HTTPRequestAbort −3`, `HTTPRequestReplacePath −4`, `NetworkDelay −6`, and the constrained fit is the next subject |
| **the formula's SUPPORT** — WHICH terms carry weight at all, as opposed to how much, since six of the fourteen ship at zero on this corpus | `weight-reachability.md` | **measured as the difference between two ceilings, not as a sweep.** Freezing the support costs `131` cases and opening it costs none, so the support is the binding constraint of the weight dimension and the values are not — which is the reverse of how this register has read the weight axis since 272 |
| **the term's per-case decision** — whether the gate that switches one term on and off is worth what it costs | `recorded-configuration.md` §3, §4 | **measured, and it is the largest single lever in the register.** The dump carries both arms, so the ablation needs no engine run: `off` 1 031, **as shipped 1 073**, `on` 1 096, and the per-case oracle **1 186 (83.40 %)**. The gate admits 108 cases (44 fixed, 2 broken) and refuses 1 114 (**111 it would have fixed, 88 it would have broken**) — the `+23` between `on` and the run is that trade, and the 111 it refuses include every one of the 231 `ReplaceCode` cases, whose rank-1 inbound rise is ~0.98 because a status-code fault fails calls rather than slowing them |
| **the zero vector as the published run** — whether `1 073` was won by tie | `recorded-configuration.md` §5 | **corrected.** The zero vector reproduces the run because with every score level the stable sort keeps the dump's order, and the dump's first candidate IS the run's answer. `Top@1` over this artifact is "the top-1 the run emitted"; ties are real and decide nothing (one case in 1 422 carries one under the shipped weights) |
| **the family gate as a constraint** — whether a vector can gain while costing no family above the 20-case floor a case | `gate-fit.md` | **measured, and it costs 89 % of the gain.** A gate-clean vector exists (nine families gain, nine unchanged, none loses, `+16/+17/+19` on three seeds) and is worth `+17.3` where the unconstrained fit is worth `+154`: **the gate's price is 137 cases**. Held out, the gain transfers (`+7` to `+22`) and the gate does not (`3` to `9` protected cases lost), because a floor stated on one corpus is not a property a parameter fit can carry |
| **the count as a linear program over the artifact** — whether `Top@1` can be maximised as an LP | `gate-fit.md` §1, §7 | **closed twice.** The zero vector answers the published run — `1 073` of `1 422`, every case by tie — so the count has a spurious optimum at the origin; and with a mandatory subsystem the problem is Max FLS, NP-hard for homogeneous bipolar systems (Amaldi & Kann, TCS 147, 1995), with no constant-factor guarantee surviving the subsystem |
| **the solver's silent pivot budget** — whether `maximise` can return an unfinished tableau as an optimum | `gate-fit.md` §2 | **a DEFECT, fixed.** A 592-row program returned `‖w‖₁ = 10.9` against a box of `1` and was read as "the gate cannot be cleared". It now throws, and the contract is asserted |
| the **`failedEdge` weight as a single value** — whether "the shipped configuration" is one configuration | `weight-reachability.md` §4, `recorded-configuration.md` §2 | **CLOSED at iteration 277, and it was not a mixture.** `failedEdge` ships at 3 and the engine records `configured × admitted(case)`, so the `0` on 1 114 cases is the gate REFUSING that case, not a configuration. Hence `w = max S` over the coefficients a dump records, and `|S| > 1` is proof a name is a decision rather than a weight. The vector every screen reported (`1 031`) never ran; the run is `1 073`, and the coefficients in the dump rebuild it exactly (0 residual mismatches in 69 688 candidates) |

## What this register holds besides its axes

Every document in `docs/` is reachable from here, because this is the one file a session is told to read  
first and a record it does not name is a record nobody finds. These are records and probes rather than axes —  
they carry no closing number, and the rows above remain the place an axis is looked up.

| `miss-reachability.md`                    | the nine per-cell windows JOINED — the quantity `latent-term-census.md` §6 names as shippable and says it cannot take offline. A weight is one number and the caps are nine, so the window is the intersection, and the second clause is the one that binds: the cap is a MINIMUM over cells and in five of eight terms the cell that sets it is a cell the term cannot pay in either. Read off battery `41188083576` on `25b4279b` the eight dormant terms hold 37 case-wins between them and **seven have no global window at all** (`collision` 0.005 against a smallest need of 0.013, `rise` 0.001 against 0.011, `source` 0.005 against 0.022, `topo` 0.008 against 0.009, `temporal` 0.010 against 0.016, `stability` 0.012 against 0.017); `prism` has one 0.005 wide `(0.008, 0.013)` bounded above by a single correct case in RE1:TrainTicket; and the ONE term with headroom is the one already armed — `dualFamily` ships at **0.25** and its cheapest win needs **0.258**, so 0.34 buys 6 cases against a cap of 0.781, a consequence of its slope being binary rather than a magnitude. That is the arithmetic behind the shape the arms keep producing ("five cells gain eight cases, three give up four"): no value of the weight separates two cells whose caps differ by 550× within one term. **AND THE ONE ARM IT AUTHORISED IS READ BACK, WITH THE WINDOW EMPTY (it.197, `docs/miss-reachability.md` §8).** `dualfam=0.34` was dispatched as `41218512485` against the push battery `41213454636` (a revision whose only difference is documentation) and reads **`644/735` against `641` — +3, and `RE1:OnlineBoutique 107 → 106`.** Both halves of the prediction are refuted (`+3` rather than `+6`, and one cell down, which is the bar every refusal here is made on), and the reason is a theorem rather than a surprise: the weight moves exactly the cases where membership is ASYMMETRIC between the truth and its challenger — all four gains are truth-member/challenger-not (`0.2576 / 0.3276 / 0.3304 / 0.3348`, every one `≤ 0.34`), and the single loss is the mirror, a correct case whose truth sits at `dualFamily 0.00` and is overtaken by a member challenger. **That case's control margin is `0.00000` to five decimals, so its cap is `0.25` — the shipped value itself — and the window is `(0.2576, 0.2500]`, which is empty.** The methodological error this retires: a cap was read as a weight ABOVE the shipped value at which a cell breaks, and a case TIED at the shipped value breaks at every value above it, so a caps table that omits `0.25` for such a case reports headroom that does not exist — a defect any term weighed against a rank surface inherits, since ties are where a rank surface puts its top. **With that, every coefficient in the sum is closed**: at its measured optimum (`selfAnomalyLog1p`), at a corner no interior point beats (`topoDiscount 1`, `gate 1`), shipped off after a measured refusal (`collision`, `prism`, `selfTime`, `victim`, `log`), or bounded by a tie at its own shipped value (`dualFamily`, `stability`) — and the 94 misses are 75 `outweighed`, which no coefficient can reach. | `fault-census.md`                         | **the axis that names an OWNER.** A cell is five fault types averaged together — `cpu`/`mem`/`disk` at 98–99%, `loss` at 61.7% — so the headline is moved by whichever population is larger and a change that trades one for another reads as noise. The line splits each type's misses three ways: `blank` (the ranking never surfaced the truth), `outweighed` (the truth's own evidence, read on the BASE term and not on the total, was strictly lower than the winner's) and `outvoted` (it was at least as high, and the entry names the term that made the difference). **75 of the 94 measurable misses are `outweighed`** across all nine cells — which is why eight iterations of weight arms moved nothing: a prior multiplies a magnitude the base term already decided. The study read RE3 at 53.33% against the golden's 58.70% for three runs and it was investigated as an input defect, until the golden's own per-fault-type columns showed the accuracies **identical in 13 of 14 comparable cells** and only the fold differing; `runners/suite-accuracy.ts` now owns both conventions and returns them together, the study reports the published one as its headline, and the one genuine residual — `run-ablation.ts` never calls `augmentTopologyWithTraces` while `run-rcaeval.ts` prunes 55–82% of the edges of every trace-bearing case — is measured at **one fault type, 2 cases, RE2 TT**. **§7 closes a residual this repair left in its OWN scope, found by an audit of the `@k` family rather than by a failing test**: §3 said "every site now calls it" and that was true of the PUBLISHED fold only — `run-ablation.ts`, the runner every ledger number comes from, kept FOUR hand-rolled case-weighted folds (`allA1`…`allTA`, each `sum(value × cases) / cases`), which §1’s own table had listed verbatim and the owner module’s docblock had named as its first offender. The guard missed it because its title was **"leaves no hand-rolled fold in the two remaining sites"** — an ENUMERATION standing in for a rule, stale since it was written. Repair: four `AccuracyCell[]` folded by `caseWeightedMean`, **bit-identical by construction** (same cells, same order, same accumulation, and the empty arm returns the `0` the removed guard returned). The stripper now has one owner (`helpers/source-text.ts`) because two fences needed it. **MEASURED (`37900344770`, `070e9b4`): the refactor is value-preserving end to end** — the three golden artifacts differ from the previous run by one `Total duration` line each, and the three ablation artifacts by 99 wall-clock tokens each, with **zero** measured values moved once timing is normalised the fold moves 77.45% -> 78.75%, +1.30 pp of which RE1 and RE3 contribute exactly 0.000; and the head-to-head gap becomes 0.16 pp = ONE case of 735 instead of 1.5 pp.** The 90 -> 180 bound was a projection of 1.8x the case-runs and is refuted by the run: `ablation-re2` measured **52.2 min**, less than the 54.3 min it took on the capped 150-case corpus, because the heap — not the corpus — was the cost. **The bound is nevertheless NOT settled at 2.1x: the identical 270-case corpus has now measured the heaviest job at 52.2 / 86.3 / 88.1 min (runs `37872246084` / `37886983273` / `37900344770`) — a 69% spread with no code path in the job changed, the last two agreeing to 2% and both differing from the first by ~65%, i.e. one observation from a regime the artifact does not record. 180 is 2.0x the observed worst case, and the operative reason is **run-to-run variance on the heaviest job**, not any projection: a bound for this job must come from the SPREAD.** Two corrections the measurement forces: `LAT WHOLE FILE` reads **Δ+0.0** on the corrected RE2 (it read +1.9 on the subset; it moves OB 86.7 -> 84.4 and TT 71.1 -> 73.3, opposite signs, mean absorbed), and the census's `logs N/M` had to be renamed because the heap filter made it count a different quantity (cases RETAINING a readable row) from the golden's identically-worded line (cases whose file yielded any row) - 21/90 against 90/90 on RE2-OB. **Two further defects surfaced while writing the acceptance.** (i) The artifact stated the AVG/CW coincidence rule TWICE — above the study's results table and above the PRISM sweep's frontier table, in different wording — so correcting one left the other still printing a claim the corrected corpus falsifies (`which is RE1 alone`; RE2 now reads AVG 83.7 vs CW 83.7 with all six fault types at 45 case-reps) ⇒ **one owner** (`FOLD_CONVENTIONS`, printed by both renderings, naming no suite), because a named answer to a population question goes stale when the population moves and a rule does not. (ii) The corpus was ranked as a SAMPLE of unrecorded composition even though the per-fault-type cells print their counts: the capped RE2 held **27 / 27 / 27 / 27 / 24 / 18** case-reps per fault type and the full one **45 x 6**, so an earlier draft's "nine of each fault type's fifteen" was not merely unverifiable but **FALSE** — and the corrected corpus is the first RE2 population this repository has held whose fault types are balanced. The fence written for (i) was itself defeated by the comments explaining (i) (the SECOND occurrence of that defect here, after the workflow sampler check), so it now reads comments-stripped source and pins the owner: `const FOLD_CONVENTIONS` exactly once, read by exactly two renderings **§8 adds the INPUT census**: `arXiv:2609.27069`'s second finding is a claim about the input — a _"non-uniform column schema that silently zeroes telemetry for 250 of 375 RE1 cases"_ — and it is **refuted against the converted corpus: 735 of 735 cases carry non-zero telemetry, 0 degenerate**, RE1 included at 375 of 375, because the bridge detects each file's own columns instead of assuming one schema. **AND THE INSTRUMENT FOUND THE SAME DEFECT IN ITSELF**: it published a per-group UNION of the service ids its cases carry that the topology does not declare, which cannot tell a name in ONE case from a name in ALL of them — RE1 OnlineBoutique showed SockShop names and RE3 SockShop showed the whole Online Boutique service set, and read as a population that is a **system swap** until the per-case distribution was asked for (the run's own artifact: 1681 services over 125 RE1-OB cases, ~13.4 per case against 11 declared). It now publishes `cases_with_foreign`, the per-case min/median/max, the **point mass** on those names, and every per-case row, with the union **named as a union**; no share is a gate, because a shared scrape is not a defect and no threshold on it is a fact. **And §8.5-8.7 (iteration 103) close the same question one artifact over**: the input census that decides STARVED from INERT returned `coverage.cases` for the METRIC channel — a CONSTRUCTION on the one channel every never-ablated prior acts on and the one a competitor's schema allegation is about — and it now MEASURES that channel from the cases themselves, reporting the LEVEL of every absence per case (`FILE-ABSENT` / `NO-POINTS` / `COLUMN-ABSENT` / `ALL-ZERO` / `NO-KEPT-ROW` / `UNREPORTED`), because the allegation's mechanism and this document's refutation have the SAME SIGNATURE in a count. The first version of the levels assigned a whole population one level and the fence's accounting invariant caught it: a census's counts must PARTITION its population. law 39. **And §8.9 answers law 40's question**: `rcaeval-loader.ts` declares at its own line 5 that **RE1 is metrics-only**, so every channel RE1 starves is starved by the DATASET's contract, and the loader already held that fact — `loadCase` calls `tryLoadLogs` / `tryLoadTraces` unconditionally, so `undefined` there means the file could not be read (`FILE-ABSENT`). **`toBenchmarkCase` destroys it one layer above** by writing `traces: undefined` deliberately for the GC, after which `undefined` means either thing. **Consequence for the standing: the reference above us on RE1 (85.4 / 82.8%) is measured on the SAME single channel, so the 5.13pp is a METHOD gap on identical input, not an input gap** — and a sentence this register had written, inferring that reference's INPUT from its METHOD, is corrected in place. **And §8.11 records what the COVERAGE standard found rather than the iterator**: iteration 104's change left one uncovered arm in `directional-evidence.ts` (100/100/100/100 at it.103 → 99.82/98.89), and writing the assertion that arm exists for showed the level it would have produced was WRONG — `ALL-ZERO` is a statement about VALUES, and every non-metric channel's `nonzero` is the count that SURVIVED retention, so the first record attached to the log or latency channel would have printed _"the readings are all zero"_ about a file that yielded forty rows and kept none. Fixed with `ChannelEvidence.carriesValues`, set `false` in the one helper every row channel reaches and **not** to `channel === 'metrics'`, a comparison no input can make (law 6). **§8.13 then closes the last `UNREPORTED` and refines law 40 in passing**: the log channel read `UNREPORTED` on 69 of RE2-OnlineBoutique's 90 cases while the same line said `21/90 readable`, because `assembleRCAEvalCase` measured `logRowsRead` and the loop never took it — and because a POPULATION-level record cannot say WHICH case held rows. The count now rides **on the case** (`BenchmarkCase.logsReadRows`), written only inside the branch that has a payload, so `NO-KEPT-ROW` / `NO-POINTS` / `UNREPORTED` are three distinct statements. **The law's missing half: the evidence must be supplied at the granularity the absence occurs at.** **And §8.10 (iteration 104) ENROLS law 40**: the census now takes each channel's HOLDER record — for the latency channel the route census's own three row counts, passed at the ablation assembly site — gains the level `RANKED-VIEW-EMPTY` for a channel that is empty on the ranked view while another view holds rows, and splits its STARVED line into `UNMEASURABLE` and `MEASURABLE-ELSEWHERE`. The unit is a slice with **two** bounds (16 cases AND 512 MiB), which is legal only because a slice is folded EXACTLY (`mergeLoadStats`/`mergeRunResults`: counts add, ratios recompute from summed numerators, samples take the first non-empty slice, census folds rows then summarises once) — and the invariance is measured, not argued: `--case-chunk 1` and `--case-chunk 16` produce the same `ss:RE2` output line for line. Then the retainer, which is the part worth remembering: after release AND collection the cell still held **1425 MB**, a heap snapshot attributed **1407 MB to 90 whole `logs.csv` strings**, and the chain was `GC roots → Stack roots → `Object.exceptionNames` → (sliced string) → parent`. A 22-character exception NAME was pinning a 22 MB document, because V8 sliced strings keep their parent. Per-cell CSV decoding fixed it (fixture: **17.02 MB → 0.14 MB** retained; cell: **1421 → 27 MB**), and the grid now finishes in **11 m 07 s at 1.28 GiB peak**, no cell above 59 MB of live heap at its Not licensed: a shared threshold (still unsupported), or shipping the RE3 router (one fitted threshold on 90 cases, no held-out validation). **Convention gap recorded**: the ceiling is case-weighted (its `perCell` grid is keyed by SYSTEM), our headline is type-mean, and the whole difference is RE3's type imbalance (58.70% vs 53.33%). Iteration 75 removed `--max-cases 50` from `benchmark-rcaeval.yml` but left the same cap in the two probe workflows its own fence had listed as legitimate samplers — and `fusion-routing-verdict.md`, a REGISTER-TRACKED VERDICT, states its union ceiling as 87.5% (538/615) and its entire routing frontier over 615 cases, i.e. over 615 of the benchmark's 735, with RE2 sampled at 150 of its 270. RE2 is the suite where the two engines disagree most, so the missing 120 cases are the ones a union estimate most needs; `delay-exhausted-verdict.md` and `rank-collapse-falsified.md` cite the same 87.5% as an information ceiling. **The fence could not catch it because it was an exact set of four filenames**: an enumeration cannot say WHY a workflow may sample, so it could not tell a probe nobody reads from a probe a verdict reads, and it was maintained by the same author about to cite the number. The rule that replaced it, over the repository's own text: **a workflow that caps its corpus may not be named by any `docs/*.md`** — population defined by invocation, not by a list, so it needs no exemption (`fse26-benchmark.yml` caps via a DISPATCH INPUT and was never a member), and it cannot go stale silently because **the day a document cites a sampler, the citation fails the assertion.** Both probes are also asserted PRESENT and uncapped, because "must not cap" alone would be satisfied by deleting the invocation. **Three mutations, three killed**: a restored cap; the invocation deleted while the comment still names the flag (the third occurrence of _a text assertion is satisfied by the comment explaining the defect_ — both probes are therefore asserted invocation-scoped, from the subcommand, the only place a flag can reach a runner); and the count-fix's own cause. **Second defect, in the artifact the ledger counts samples from:** `run-ablation.ts` allocates the per-fault-type accumulator OUTSIDE the repetition loop and accumulates INSIDE it, so every printed `(n)` is `cases x REPETITIONS` (RE1 375 vs 125, RE2 270 vs 90, RE3 90 vs 30) — the number is right, its UNIT was missing, and it sat three lines from a `(n cases)` line printed by the same artifact, **two quantities one word**, which is why the ledger (`ABLATION_FINDINGS`, internal docs repo) v8 records capped RE2 as `27/27/27/27/24/18` (= `9/9/9/9/8/6` cases) and full RE2 as `45x6` (= `15x6`). The header states the unit now and the test pins the STATEMENT and its CAUSE. This is the unit-contract census the register has carried as a next step since iteration 75, and it found one on its first field |

The frontier is therefore still `{w=0}`, and the reason is structural rather than tuned: an ADDED score reorders every candidate, while the axiom only has something to say about the ones that FAIL it. So the term built here is `−victimWeight × (1 − symmetry) × log1p(selfAnomaly)` with `symmetry = 2·min(Sⁱ,Sᵉ)/(Sⁱ+Sᵉ)` — a ratio, so no threshold had to be invented; `1` for a component with NO internal channel, because an axiom about internal properties cannot be applied to a component that carries none; and neutral on a case where every candidate is external-only, which is what RE1's `delay`/`loss` cells are. Ships at 0 with the map unbuilt. **MEASURED AND REFUSED at the FIRST weight**: `victim=0.05` costs **33** cases on RE1 (290/375, TrainTicket 101 → 68) and `0.50` costs 106 (217), while FSE'26 at 0.2 reads Top@1 **55.0%** against 56.4%. Online Boutique and Sock Shop are untouched at EVERY weight and RE3 is unchanged — the density signature again — because `sym` ratios two incommensurable quantities (a resource shift ~0.1σ against a transport shift ~4σ), so the discount is near-uniform on 13 edges and violently non-uniform on 79, where the survivors are the CALLERS retrying. **The PRISM family is therefore CLOSED in THREE forms with one cause** (additive −10 RE1 for +12 fold, conjunctive −37 for RE3-TT 15 → 24, mask −33): all three re-weight a tuned ranking by a z-score whose scale no other term controls |

| `self-time-share.md` | **the mechanism the row above names, built and shipped OFF.** A caller's response time CONTAINS its callees', so `share(v) = max(0, L(v) − max over callees c of L(c)) / L(v)` separates a transport rise a node CREATED from one it INHERITED, where `L` is a latency channel's `log₁₀(1 + rise)` over the median of the first and last thirds of the RAW series — raw because the guards delete exactly the propagation channels the comparison needs, which is why a service is ABSENT rather than zero when its channel is unmeasurable or when any callee's is. `topoSource` and its falsified mirror read TOTAL anomaly and ask "is this node explained by a neighbour"; this reads the TRANSPORT channel and asks how much of the delay nothing downstream accounts for, so a leaf keeps its whole rise by DEFINITION rather than by the degree artefact the topological term inherits. Ships at `DEFAULT_SELF_TIME_WEIGHT = 0` with the map not built, dispatchable as `selftime=` / `self_time_weight=` so both halves of the kill criterion are measurable. **MEASURED AND REFUSED**: `selftime=0.1` costs **48** cases on RE1 (271/375) and `0.3` costs **50** (269), with TrainTicket 98 → 47 → 42 while Online Boutique and Sock Shop GAIN — the leaf-1.0 property is a hub penalty on a 64-service/79-edge graph, and the term is a graph-DENSITY bias rather than a source signal. What survives is the requirement: a share must be compared against the FLEET's typical share, not against absolute `[0, 1]` |

A TEXT fence that demanded the _name_ `meanOverFaultTypes` in `run-rcaeval.ts` — and was satisfied by the block that printed one number four times — became a VALUE fence on the fold |
| `fault-type-identification.md` | **type accuracy (`TA`) was zero by construction, and the table hid it by printing the `AC@1` column under the `TA` label.** `RootCauseResult.faultType` came from `classifyFaultType(score, depth, childContribution)` — a SEVERITY descriptor (`CPU`/`MEMORY`/`CONNECTION_POOL`/`CODE_ERROR`/`UNKNOWN`) that never looks at which metric moved, so it could not equal a ground-truth label (`cpu`/`mem`/`disk`/`delay`/`loss`/`socket`) on any case. `StatisticalAnalyzer` — Layer 2 of the classifier pyramid, which emits exactly that vocabulary — had **never been called from the RCA path**, and wiring it exposed three defects inside it: `minDataPoints` was compared with the NUMBER OF SERIES rather than with a series' length (so a service carrying one or two series was refused as `UNKNOWN`), `trendSlope` was a per-sample ABSOLUTE slope so the `trendStrength > 0.3` rule was a statement about units (**383** for a latency series, 0.004 for a cpu one — `DELAY` was the only category it could emit, measured on every service of every case), and two rules can fire on one series with the bigger confidence formula winning (a monotone ramp is both `MEM`@0.60 and `CPU`@0.79). The hypothesis is now the dominant metric's FAMILY first — definitional links, not fitted ones — with the shape rules as the fallback, and the evidence string says which answered. **RE1-OnlineBoutique TA 0.0 → 43.2** (cpu 92.0, delay 100.0, mem 24.0, disk 0.0, loss 0.0) with **AC@1 byte-identical at 82.4**, which is the acceptance criterion for a type-only change. `disk` and `loss` stay at zero and the reason is the corpus: RE1 ships no disk-I/O and no packet-loss series, and `log`/`lat` are `INPUT_MAP_EMPTY` on all 374 cases — the two labels are unidentifiable from what that suite carries, which is also why its disk and loss LOCALIZATION columns are the weak ones |
| `topological-source-direction.md` | **the topological-source term explained a node by its CALLER; a caller is what waits.** `computeTopoSourceScores` shipped `1 − max over PARENTS of (w(p→v)×a(p))`, so on a graph where `u → v` means u CALLS v it penalised the source (whose caller is anomalous) and rewarded the symptom. Its own option docblock had carried the caveat since it was written — _"resource faults can propagate callee → caller, in which case this directed penalty would misfire"_ — and the same arrays were being read with opposite conventions in two places, with nothing declaring which. **Measured on RE1-OnlineBoutique, one variable: at weight 0.5 the old sign reads 57.6 (−24.8 pp) and the corrected sign 82.4; at 0.1 the corrected sign reads 85.6 (+3.2 pp) with NO fault type regressed** (delay 88→92, disk 92→100, mem 92→96, cpu and loss unmoved). It also explains the term's own case verdict: **−42.4 / −37.8 / −3.1 on FSE'26's three suites were taken with the sign this table calls backwards**. The correction is **behaviour-neutral where it ships** (`DEFAULT_TOPO_WEIGHT` is 0, and at weight zero every direction is the same function — measured 82.4 before and after, cell for cell), which is the condition under which a sign may be fixed without a dispatch. **The WEIGHT is not enrolled**: the corrected curve has no plateau (85.6 / 84.8 / 84.8 / 83.2 / 82.4) and a maximum at the smallest positive weight tested is the signature of a weak signal; the nine-cell and FSE'26 readings decide it. **THE READING LANDED AND THE WEIGHT IS REFUSED:** at 0.1 with everything else shipped, run `40167961908` reads RE1-OnlineBoutique **85.6 (+3.2)**, RE1-SockShop 92.8 (0), **RE1-TrainTicket 28.8 (−46.4)**, RE2-OB 85.6 (+1.2), RE2-SS 91.1 (−1.1), RE2-TT 62.2 (−12.2), RE3-SS 48.6 (+1.1), and FSE'26 55.8 (−0.3), i.e. **RE1 83.47 → 69.07**. The mechanism is a UNIT and not a signal: on OnlineBoutique the anomaly is a raw score of order 1–3, so a [0,1] term at 0.1 is a nudge against gaps of ~0.3; on TrainTicket 63–69 nodes trip `anomalyNormalizeNodeThreshold` and the anomaly is rank-normalised into steps of **1/63 = 0.0159**, so the same term moves a node up to **six rank steps** and replaces the ranking instead of nudging it. The named successor is a MULTIPLICATIVE discount, `a'(v) = a(v)·(1 − ρ·(1 − topoSource(v)))`, which is dimensionless and therefore means the same thing on both scales, with a falsifiable prediction: the truth is the source and the winner is a caller, so TT should move UP where the additive form moved it down 46 pp |

The units make the population law visible from the other end: on TrainTicket the charges are 1–7 positions of a 63-step rank surface (`0.1111 = 7 steps`, `0.0794 = 5`, `0.0476 = 3`) while on OnlineBoutique and SockShop the same action deletes 95–99.8 % of a deviation. **So the closure is by information set, not by score**: `rho`, `gate`, `scope` and `closure` all move that one charge between a caller and its callee, the arm's expectation is the base rate at which a charged caller happens to be the culprit, and the measured plane (`631 → 635 → 637/635/636 → 641`) is that rate rising as the charge is restricted to complete explanations — `share = 1` is the only confidence the operator can express that pays, and it is the shipped value. Fenced by `gate-arm-census.test.ts`, which joins §7.1's cell table to §7.2's case table row for row and goes red when either is edited without the other. | |
