than of any signal. The `earliest-only` shape **does** have an admissible window (**+4, 0
lost**) and is the axis's open candidate, with the pair as the next measurement. Read those
three rows before proposing anything on a TIME; the free read is one command and it is
already run, so a proposal that has not re-run it has not engaged the measurement.

**The onset candidate has since been measured and rejected, and the instrument that
judged it has been repaired.** `earliest-only` passed the FSE'26 half (+4 cases, zero
regressed fault types, the four datapacks the solver named in advance) and moved six of
the nine golden cells, so it was reverted (`docs/fse26-onset-verdict.md` §8). Two
iterations later the log-term reconstruction turned out to divide by the SUM of two
overlapping signature sets where the engine divides by their UNION — which deflated
every competing score in every case with a framework-HTTP flood, and which the
instrument had been printing as its own "error bar" (`docs/fse26-log-flood-verdict.md`).
That is worth reading as one story rather than two: **a mode pre-screen drawn from a
wrong denominator was used as evidence about a signal**, and the guard rail that would
have caught it — "the reconstruction must reproduce the dump's own mode, case for case"
— is now printed by the tool rather than assumed by its readers.

The instrument's reach at the shipped configuration is now measured rather than
inferred: the reconstruction reproduces the run's own rank-1 **1422/1422**, the routing
map is complete, and **221 of the 666 misses are silent on both sides**, which is larger
than any single term's attributable share. A candidate that has not said which of those
it addresses has not engaged the map.

**And a candidate must now say what its ARTIFACT carries** (`docs/artifact-capability-audit.md`). Three
iterations each found, by hand, a claim resting on a quantity its artifact does not hold — a precision
nobody declared, a population that was a subset, a composition the named run never rendered — and the
generalisation is an instrument: `scripts/dump_capability.py` reports every channel as `every` / `some` /
`none`, over the artifact's own case and row counts, and refuses a read the artifact cannot serve.

Two facts from it bear directly on the lever above, and both are about the artifacts rather than about the
engine:

- The FSE'26 dump this record reads (`35035314921`, 1422 cases, 72527 rows) carries **no declared precision,
  no decisive composition and no `both=`** — 141 MB in which `metricDecisive` appears zero times. A
  composition-based candidate is **UNEVALUABLE** there and must name the artifact that carries it, exactly as
  the stability rows had to name `35107871516`.
- Where the decisive composition does exist it reaches **`some`**, not `every` — 86.45% of `re1`'s rows,
  90.72% of `re3`'s — while the field's own comment opened by claiming it "exists for EVERY service". A term
  built on the composition has to be simulated over _every_ candidate a case could promote, so its
  precondition is a **producer change**, and that is now what the comment says instead of the claim it
  contradicted two sentences later.

A candidate that has not named the channels it reads, the reach it needs of each, and the artifact — by run
— it reads them from, has not engaged this either.

**And the reach is now TWO numbers, because the composition's own line stopped being selective.** The
producer renders `metricDecisive` on **every** row now (the `-` marker where the named metric carries no
decomposition, the same marker `onset` and `latRise` use), so the channel is universal while the composition
itself reaches **98.13%** of the shipped artifact's rows (`71161/72527`) — and the 1566 rows that used to
carry no line at all were exactly the rows whose inventory is not rendered either, so their absence was
unattributable. A candidate must therefore say whether it needs the channel or the VALUE: `onset` is the
warning, reaching every row and carrying a number on **87.5%** of them.

**And it must now say WHICH HALF OF A FAMILY, because the census's own population was seven hand-written
channels against the artifact's thirty-one fields** (`docs/artifact-capability-audit.md` Finding 7). Both
two-part families were covered in the half the OTHER one covers: `failed-edge` read the SCORE, leaving
`edgeRecords`' COUNT — the one signal the separator verdict reports as HOLDING, **0.908** where the score reads
**0.457** — with no channel, and `latency-edges` read the COUNT, leaving the `lat` term's RISE with none and
reporting the other half's reach (**100%** against the rise's **52.0%**). Six quantities the declared signals
read had no channel at all, so the gate above could not be satisfied by the candidates this record calls live.
The population is a table whose key column is the producer's own literal with each marker DERIVED from it
(which is how the drift happened: one pattern was written for `latEdges` and used for a `latRise` read), held
by two fences on a two-edge chain — the python test keeps the committed projection equal to the table, and the
TypeScript test builds a dump with the PRODUCER and holds the emitted keys, the table's `fields` and
`Object.keys(SERVICE_FIELD_AUDIT)` equal in both directions. **A candidate that names `failed-edge` for a count
read, or `latency-edges` for a rise read, is naming the other half of the pair and will be told the other
half's reach.** For the inventory the halves are not even the same LINE: `metric-kept`/`metric-drop` reach 1888
of `re1`'s rows, `metric-top` 1887, and `artifacts/diag-34684319273` carries the first pair for 2095 rows and
the second not at all.

**And a channel's reach is not its VALUE, because one grammar carries two quantities.** A declaration that
names a channel without naming WHERE on the line its value sits is the same defect as one that names the wrong
channel: the producer writes `metricKept(N): <list>` and writes the list only while `N > 0`, so a rendered
**zero** is a measurement whose list is absent — read from the list instead, it came back as "rendered and
undetermined" on **9 readings over 7 artifacts** while the READER reads the parenthesised number and the
producer's own doc says `both=0` "is NEVER omitted because it is zero"
(`docs/artifact-capability-audit.md` Finding 8). The placement is therefore a **stated** column
(`field` / `paren` / `body`), the marker is still derived, and the **third edge** of the fence closes it —
**the census's valuation against the READER's own parse of the same artifact** — because the two edges that
existed were both satisfied by the wrong form: the table was self-consistent and the reader was correct. The
projection carries the census's own `pattern`, `valueIn` and `absent` so the other side applies the SAME regex
rather than re-deriving it, and a re-derived one is how a fence whose halves disagree about what a line means
passes on its own bug.

**And the criterion itself is now an intersection rather than a comparison in prose.** Its two halves live on
two benchmarks — a candidate must GAIN on one and cost another nothing — so the object it asks for is the
intersection of two sets of WEIGHTS, and the record compared them by hand four times, three of them ending up
with a number the artifacts did not support. One command now computes it (`criterionReadings` +
`criterionVerdicts` + `formatCriterionReport`, by repeating `--dump`, each artifact solved on its own
population and in its own box). **The halves are ASYMMETRIC and the readings now say so**: the artifact named
FIRST is the one a candidate must improve and every other is one it must leave untouched, because a first
version that took a `min` across all of them produced a wrong headline in BOTH directions — it credited a gain
on the protected half (temporal `earliness` "admissible" from `0.001664`, a weight at which nothing on the
gain side moves) and it folded the gain artifact's OWN permission into the protected side's ceiling, which
falsely closed the stability axis. Corrected, the stability axis has an admissible region on BOTH shapes —
`flip` `[0.004134, 0.007528)` and `rank` `[0.006672, 0.008032)`, each worth ONE case, with FSE'26's own tie
class permitting a loss from `0.003873` as the one bar a run must settle — while the TEMPORAL intersection is
empty on all four shapes: `earliest-only` is the only one whose FSE'26 gain is free on FSE'26, and the golden
caps that shape at `0.004717`, **2.2× below the first weight at which FSE'26 gains anything there** and 7.7×
below the `0.036552` the solver recommended. **A proposal that spans both benchmarks must state its
intersection, name each artifact's role, and it can now be computed rather than argued.** **And the first
candidate it named has now CLEARED BOTH HALVES and been ENROLLED** (`fse26-cv-screen.md` §"The dispatched criterion verdict"):
`stabilityWeight=0.007352` on `2f10a82` — the `rank` region's midpoint — gives FSE'26 **757/1422 = 53.23%**
(was 756), Top@3 66.5%, Top@5 70.4%, **0 regressed fault types** (`HTTPResponseReplaceCode 160 → 161` is the
only move), with the RCAEval golden **9 of 9 byte-identical** (`35411810992`). The prediction was **+1** and
the run delivered +1 case for case. **So the stability axis's re-opening condition is MET and the term has been ENROLLED**: `DEFAULT_STABILITY_WEIGHT`
is now `0.007352`, guarded as text and required to be a key of `MEASURED_STABILITY_WEIGHTS` with BOTH halves
recorded, alongside the REJECTED `0.030170` kept as data. **And it has now walked the DEFAULT path**: run
`35416576350` passes no input at all and reads `stabilityWeight=0.007352` off the constant, giving `757/1422`
against the same-commit control `35416580279` at `756` — one case, `HTTPResponseReplaceCode 160 → 161`, nothing
moving the other way — with the push's own golden (`35416556932`) 9 of 9 byte-identical. That is the
`defaultPath` sub-record, and the guard now requires it: a point measured by passing a flag is a measurement
of the flag and not of what ships.

**AND THE CLOSURE HAS NOW BEEN RE-SOLVED IN A TEN-TIMES-FINER BOX, which is the one thing those numbers had
never been asked.** Every window above was computed from a dump rendered at three decimals, and the two
preceding iterations proved twice over that a finer render MOVES a window rather than refining it. There is
now a four-decimal FSE'26 artifact of the SAME 1422 cases (run `35436069639`, identical fault-type
histogram), so the gain half was re-solved in it against the identical golden protect half:

| gain artifact         | `flip`                                                         | `rank`                                                         |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 3 dec (`35107871516`) | gains from `0.004134`, `[0.004134, 0.007528)` width `0.003395` | gains from `0.006672`, `[0.006672, 0.008032)` width `0.001360` |
| 4 dec (`35436069639`) | gains from `0.003765`, `[0.003765, 0.007528)` width `0.003764` | gains from `0.006096`, `[0.006096, 0.008032)` width `0.001937` |

**`0.007352` is inside BOTH shapes' regions in BOTH boxes, so the weight is not box-fragile and the axis stays
closed.** Only the GAIN end moves; both ceilings are identical (`0.007528` from `re2`, `0.008032` from `re1`)
because the protect half is the same three-decimal golden in both invocations — a clean decomposition worth
stating: **a window's gain end is a function of the gain artifact's box, its ceiling a function of the protect
artifacts' box.** The finer render widens the region at the gain end rather than narrowing it (`flip`
`0.004134 → 0.003765`, `rank` `0.006672 → 0.006096`), so what moves is not admissibility but the weight's
POSITION in it: `0.007352` is the `rank` region's midpoint at three decimals (50.0% up) and sits 64.8% up the
finer one. **The midpoint rationale is therefore box-dependent and the weight is not** — and the weight is
what the criterion asks about, since the render is a dump-only parameter that moves no cell (the same
dispatch that produced this dump is 9 of 9 golden byte-identical and reports `correct at 0 756`, unchanged).
A candidate at the finer midpoint `0.007064` is a NAMED follow-up, not a re-opening: it would have to clear
the criterion's own two halves by a dispatch, and the criterion is satisfied where the weight already is.

**AND THE PRISM SIGNAL'S SECOND KNOB IS NOW AN OPEN AXIS RATHER THAN AN UNREACHABLE ONE**
(`docs/prism-pooling-axis.md`). `conjunctive` was implemented in `combinePrismScore` and measured by the
standalone evaluator, while the engine's single call site omitted the pooling — so no engine run, ablation row
or dispatch could select it, and the `conjunctive` column of `prism-head-to-head.md` §2 was reproducible from
no engine configuration at all. `TreePrunerOptions.prismPooling` (`--prism-pooling`) now names it, the value
rides the reported line, and the ablation battery carries the two pooling rows as the additive rows' siblings.

It is OPEN, and the reason is in the cells rather than in the average. On the identical 735 cases of run
`34246577708`, `additive` wins **7 of the 9 cells** — every resource-fault cell of RE1 and RE2 — while
`conjunctive` wins **exactly 2, both RE3**: RE3 TrainTicket **76.7% against 33.3%** (+43.4pp, the largest
single-cell margin anywhere in this record, on the weakest cell of the published nine) and RE3 OnlineBoutique
+3.3pp. Overall it is 69.8% against 78.9% (−9.1pp), because it collapses RE1 OnlineBoutique to 51.2% (−32.8).
**A global choice is unsupportable in either direction**, so the axis belongs to the same per-case
discriminator the paragraphs above arrive at from the other end — and unlike them, its question has never been
asked inside the engine.

**Its closure needs one more thing, and it is no longer the thing this sentence used to name.** It read: _"The flag
is accepted by the RCAEval runner and reachable from **no workflow** (recorded in `UNDISPATCHABLE_ON_RCAEVAL`), so a
candidate that ships a per-context pooling rule has an undecidable golden half until a `prism_pooling` dispatch input
exists"_ — and **neither half of that is true as of iteration 95**: `prism_pooling` is a `workflow_dispatch` input of
`benchmark-rcaeval.yml` and `--prism-pooling` is passed by all seven of its suites, and the flag is a member of no
such set (`UNDISPATCHABLE_ON_RCAEVAL` holds four: `--fusion-ceiling`, `--rank-normalization` and the two negated
suppression poles). It was corrected in iteration 100, which found the claim by asking whether a DOCUMENT may state a
flag's reach at all — it may not, because the workflow owns that fact, which is the same law as iteration 98's default
owner and iteration 99's artefact availability. **A candidate's golden half is decidable now**, so what this axis waits
on is the per-case discriminator rather than a dispatch; `ABLATION_FINDINGS` (the internal ledger) v8 measures it at **+29.0 pp on RE3**
against additive's +16.2 and **−3.5 pp on RE1**, which is a two-population structure and not a global choice.

## The one axis this register lists as OPEN, and why it is not a fifth knob

**THE SET A RANKING IS A RANKING OF (it.167, `docs/pool-admission.md`).** Every row above is a coefficient that
was moved and refused, and §7.3 of `docs/topo-discount-scope.md` closed the whole family on arithmetic: weight,
gate, scope and closure are four descriptions of `min(a_v, e_v)`, and no value of any of them changes that form.
What none of them touched is the **denominator** — `performTreeRCA` admits a node only when its post-deduction
self-anomaly is positive, so the pool is `{v : selfScore(v) > 0}` and not the graph, and a node the operator
explains in full is **absent rather than last**. Twelve of the 94 misses in the published arm are a truth of
exactly that shape (`truthInGraph: true`, `truthRank: null`), which is why this is the first axis in this file
recorded as `OPEN` rather than closed: it has not been read back on the nine cells, and both comments that called
the pool the graph — `run-rcaeval.ts` in it.166 and `loss-census.ts` in it.167 — were stating the wrong object in
the one place an artifact is read from. **The two-cell local readback (§8 of that document) already refutes the
CAUSAL half of §7.4's sentence**: the single absent truth there reads `truthAnomalyBefore = 0`, i.e. it was silent
and no callee could have explained it, and the count of absent-with-a-positive-anomaly across 155 cases is zero.
So the axis is open on the SET and closed on the attribution.

**READ BACK (it.167, `docs/pool-admission.md` §9): the mechanism is complete and the magnitude is not, so the arm
is NOT enrolled.** Two arms on `ff965bc4` — bare control `41113102918` (641/735, reproducing the published total
cell for cell) and `anomaly_knobs=pooladmission=graph` `41113107920` (**642/735**, every cell at or above the control,
RE1:OnlineBoutique the only mover at +1). The census splits the twelve: **six `silent` and six `explained`**, all
twelve recovered to a rank, **one** recovered to rank 1, and `rca_score = 0` on **twelve of twelve** — so every
recovered candidate is ordered by priors alone, and eight of the twelve carry a prior worth ≤ 0.56 while four
carry 0.0028, 0.0012, 0.0011, 0 and 0. The class is real, is HALF SILENCE, and cannot be reached by admitting more
nodes; +0.14 pp against a 1.2 pp standard error is why `DEFAULT_POOL_ADMISSION` stays `positive`. The ruling also
records a defect of the pre-registered rule rather than patching it: the rule vetoed on P1/P3 and both passed, so
by its letter the arm was never refused while the only quantity about whether to ship it missed its bar — the
total belongs in the veto set, and the next arm's rule says so.

It is **not** a fifth knob of the deduction, and the distinction is the reason it survives the closure: the four
knobs scale or gate one TERM, whereas `poolAdmission` changes which nodes the terms apply to. The arm is
`pooladmission=graph` on both dispatch surfaces, its predictions and refusal rule are written in
`docs/pool-admission.md` §6 before any arm exists, and the instrument that makes it readable — `truthAnomalyBefore`
plus `classifyTruthAbsence`'s six answers — ships in the same commit so a total cannot be published without the
classification that explains it.

**THE INJECTION-ANCHORED TEMPORAL PRIOR IS CLOSED AS A GLOBAL CONSTANT, AND THE ARM THAT CLOSES IT WAS CHOSEN ONE CELL
TOO LATE** (`docs/latent-term-census.md` §7–§8).

`temporalWeight = 0.02` was dispatched against a control on the same SHA — control `41172335109` at 0.0, arm
`41172340473` at 0.02, both `6bd27da3`. The control reproduced the shipped nine cells **exactly** (RE1 85.6 / 93.6 /
84.8, RE3 88.9 / 63.6 / 74.5, all six identical to the push battery's own), which is what makes the arm's reading
causal rather than a second sample: **RE1-OnlineBoutique 85.6 → 86.4** (+1 case, the LOSS column 52.0 → 56.0),
**RE1-TrainTicket 84.8 → 85.6** (+1, LOSS 48.0 → 52.0), **RE2-TrainTicket 83.3 → 82.2** (−1, DISK 93.3 → 86.7),
**RE3-TrainTicket 74.5 → 71.0** (−1, CPU 100.0 → 85.7), and the other five cells byte-identical: **+2 cases against
−2, a wash that leaves the nine-cell total at exactly 641/735 = 87.21%**. The pre-registered criterion for this axis
was _ship only on a zero-regression body_, so a body that redistributes without improving closes the axis rather than
shipping it — and the fit that would keep the two gains and drop the two losses is exactly what the criterion forbids.
The first read of this arm covered six cells because RE2's job had not finished, and it said "net +1": the correction
is recorded here rather than quietly applied, because a partial battery is a number that looks like a result.

**Why it cannot be tuned into a zero-regression body is arithmetic, and all three runs carry it.** Of the 66 misses
whose direction is decided, the term points the right way on **25** and the wrong way on **41** — and the split is per
CELL: RE1-OnlineBoutique **5 / 7**, RE1-SockShop **0 / 2**, RE1-TrainTicket **9 / 6**, RE2-OnlineBoutique **1 / 2**,
RE2-SockShop **0 / 0**, RE2-TrainTicket **7 / 6**, RE3-OnlineBoutique **1 / 0**, RE3-SockShop **2 / 10**,
RE3-TrainTicket **0 / 8**. The arm gained anyway, because a gain needs the term to be right only WHERE THE GAP IS
CHEAP: the two positive cells' cheapest requirements are **0.016** and **0.017** with caps **0.123** and **0.069**, so
their windows overlap on **[0.017, 0.069)** and 0.02 sits at the floor of that intersection. The loss comes from the
cells with no evidence at all: on RE3-TrainTicket the term reads the truth higher than the winner on **0 of 8**
misses, so its window there is empty at EVERY weight and any weight above its cap is pure risk — the cap is **0.010**,
which the shipped battery of `63c761a6` now prints for that cell as `temporal(cap=0.010,need=none)`. **A term can
break even while pointing right on 25 of 66 decided misses, because the right cases are the cheap ones** — RE1 decides
29 and the term is right on 14, RE2 decides 16 and it is right on 8, RE3 decides 21 and it is right on 3 — which is
why "is the prior accurate" was the wrong question and the gap/slope arithmetic is the right one.

**The sibling arm also corrects the reason the previous one was refused.** `41165874503` ran `temporal_weight=0.05,
onset_shape=earliest-only` and lost **16 cases on RE1-TrainTicket and 5 on RE3-TrainTicket**, which was read as "the
pull scales with the candidate pool, so the term needs normalising by graph size". These two runs do not support that
reading: **RE1-TrainTicket is the same 68-node graph and it GAINED a case at 0.02**, so node count does not separate
the cell that gains from the cell that loses. What separates them is the SIGN, and it belongs to the fault regime
rather than to the graph: RE1 is 14 right against 15 wrong across its three cells, RE2 is 8 against 8, and RE3 is 3
against 18 — on RE3-TrainTicket alone **0 against 8**. Both cells that lost are **RE2-TrainTicket and
RE3-TrainTicket**, and on both the arm's own run puts the cheapest requirement at **0.212** while a case was lost at a
weight of 0.02: the cap is under the weight and the requirement is ten times above it, which is a window that is empty
at every weight below 0.21 — the exact reading the `shut:` segment now prints instead of dropping. Pool normalisation
would fix the loudness of a term whose sign is already right; it cannot fix a term that is inverted on the cell it is
applied to. The two successors are therefore different experiments — normalise for the scale, discriminate for the
sign — and only the second can reach the cell that produced this loss.

**The instrument failed on the one cell that decided the arm, and it is fixed rather than noted.** `[latent]` built
its head from the terms with `flips > 0` and FILTERED OUT the rest, so the decisive reading on RE3-TrainTicket — `cap
= 0.010, need = none`, i.e. a price with no upside — was dropped before the head was taken. The dispatch then chose
0.02 with no line saying the loss was coming, and the arm was the first place the number appeared. The line now
carries a second segment ordered by the smallest CAP (the cell's weight budget) and counting its own truncation, so a
term with a price and no evidence cannot be invisible again:

[latent] misses=8 guarded=22 | win: none | shut: temporal(cap=0.005,need=none) ...

The same two runs also cross-validate the census against an offline replay of the artifacts: recomputing each miss's
requirement from `top1Terms` + `truthEvidence` reproduces the in-run `temporal=1(0.123,0.016)` on RE1-OnlineBoutique
and `temporal=3(0.069,0.017)` on RE1-TrainTicket to the printed digit, so the reading is a function of the artifact
and not of the run that wrote it.

**And the reading is now a PRE-flight check rather than a post-mortem.** The shipped battery prints the temporal
prior's own window on every cell, and the arm's nine-cell outcome is a function of those six numbers:

| cell               | temporal `cap`          | cheapest `need` | window               | arm at 0.02 |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | --------------- | -------------------- | ----------- |
| RE1-OnlineBoutique | 0.123                   | 0.016           | `[0.016, 0.123)`     | gains 1     |
| RE1-SockShop       | 0.070                   | none            | empty                | unchanged   |
| RE1-TrainTicket    | 0.069                   | 0.017           | `[0.017, 0.069)`     | gains 1     |
| RE3-OnlineBoutique | 0.049                   | none            | empty                | unchanged   |
| RE3-SockShop       | not in the printed head | 0.905           | empty                | unchanged   |
| RE3-TrainTicket    | **0.010**               | none            | **below the weight** | loses 1     |

Five of the six caps are in the lines the battery already printed. RE3-SockShop's is not, because that cell's head is
ordered by cap and its temporal entry sits below the third row — the row above says what the line says rather than
what the cell implies. RE2's three land when its job does, and the verdict above does not depend on them. A weight can
be chosen against this table before a dispatch is spent, which is the difference between an instrument and a
scoreboard.

What the axis waits on is unchanged and is now stated in one number per cell: a **per-case discriminator** that
recognises the RE1-like onset signature before the weight is applied. That is the same conclusion the pool-family row
and the prism-pooling row reach from their own ends, and it is the only lever the 88.9%-reachable paragraph at the top
of this register leaves open.

**THE WEIGHT-SEARCH AXIS IS CLOSED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT BY A NINTH ARM** (`docs/fault-census.md`).

The census prices every miss against the candidate that beat it, on the BASE term rather than on the total:
`finalScore = log1p(selfAnomaly) + Σ wᵢ·signalᵢ`, and every prior is multiplied by a magnitude the base term has
already decided. Measured on all nine cells — `RE1`, `RE2` and `RE3` across all three systems, 735 cases —
**75 of the 94 misses are `outweighed`** (79.8%), against **12 `blank`** and **7 `outvoted`**. Per cell, misses and the
weighed/blank/outvoted split:

| cell                 | n       | pooled     | published | miss   | outweighed | blank  | outvoted |
| -------------------- | ------- | ---------- | --------- | ------ | ---------- | ------ | -------- |
| `RE1:OnlineBoutique` | 125     | 85.6%      | 85.6%     | 18     | 16         | 1      | 1        |
| `RE1:SockShop`       | 125     | 93.6%      | 93.6%     | 8      | 6          | 2      | 0        |
| `RE1:TrainTicket`    | 125     | 84.8%      | 84.8%     | 19     | 15         | 0      | 4        |
| `RE2:OnlineBoutique` | 90      | 92.2%      | 92.2%     | 7      | 3          | 4      | 0        |
| `RE2:SockShop`       | 90      | 97.8%      | 97.8%     | 2      | 0          | 2      | 0        |
| `RE2:TrainTicket`    | 90      | 83.3%      | 83.3%     | 15     | 14         | 0      | 1        |
| `RE3:OnlineBoutique` | 30      | 83.3%      | 88.9%     | 5      | 2          | 3      | 0        |
| `RE3:SockShop`       | 30      | 60.0%      | 63.6%     | 12     | 11         | 0      | 1        |
| `RE3:TrainTicket`    | 30      | 73.3%      | 74.5%     | 8      | 8          | 0      | 0        |
| **total**            | **735** | **87.21%** | —         | **94** | **75**     | **12** | **7**    |

The two rate columns are different units, and the difference is the same problem one level down: `pooled` is cases
over cases, while `published` is the unweighted mean of the per-type rates — so on `RE3:OnlineBoutique` a three-case
type carries the same weight as a ten-case one and the cell reads 88.9% against a pooled 83.3%.

The consequence is not a new hypothesis; it is a retirement. A weight on a dormant term can only move a candidate by
`Δw × slope`, and on these cells it must also overcome a base-term deficit that is already larger than the gaps the
latent census priced. That is why the two arms the latent census predicted came back at **+2/−2** and **+2/−1/−1**:
they were aimed at the one bucket the corpus does not populate — **seven** cases in 735, one or none per cell,
against 75 that no weight can reach.

The seven `outvoted` cases are therefore the whole of the reachable population, and they name two terms and no others:
`dualFamily` on all seven, `stability` on five. Both are the formula's only magnitude-free signals — a flat `0.25` for
being instrumented in two metric families, and an ordinal rank in `[0, 1]` over the candidates' dispersion bonus. That
is the clue the next iteration starts from rather than a result. Two numbers bound its worth: the bonus is `0.25` against a base term whose whole range is
`log1p(1) = 0.693` on a rank-normalised graph — 36% of the measured range — and the rescaling that removes
cross-service scale has already run on the large system, where **37 of 42** misses are `outweighed` all the same (88.1%),
against **38 of 52** (73.1%) on the small ones. The deficit is the ordering, not the scale.

What the axis was standing in for is the question this census makes askable and the previous ones could not: **why is
the truth quieter?** On `loss` the injected service's own tail latency rises a median **1.86×** against **12.6×** for
`disk` and **46×** for `mem`, and the channel that carries it survives the guards — **1** of 12 misses loses a strong
channel to `transient-return`, so this is not a filtering defect. It is that the injected service's own measurement is
genuinely weaker than the propagated symptom's, which is a statement about comparability across services and about how
the formula prices the two magnitude-free signals it already has, not about the ranking formula.

## Iteration 240 — the guard's vocabulary had two owners, and the second one was six words long

This is a closure rather than an axis, and it is recorded here because it is the reason a pre-registered axis
would have stayed open for a reason that has nothing to do with measurement.

Iteration 239 added the seventh member (`hump`) to `TRANSIENT_GUARD_TESTS` and closed with one sentence of
pre-registration: read it on the nine golden cells and on FSE'26. The golden half routes the flag as a
passthrough and reaches the CLI, which validates against the union. `fse26-benchmark.yml`'s `ranking_knobs`
carried its own copy of the six older members, so `ranking_knobs=transient_guard_test=hump` exited **before the
engine was built**, with a message that listed the copy. Seven in the table, six in the branch.

The repair is subtraction, not addition: the branch forwards `"$value"` and the terminal check is the CLI's,
against `Object.keys(TRANSIENT_GUARD_TESTS)` — the same check both parsers already had, and the one
`fse26-cli.test.ts` already iterates so a new member cannot be unparseable on that half. The golden half's seven
branch comments also stopped naming members; each said `` `endpoint` … and ships ``, which stopped being true the
iteration the default moved to `evidence-trimmed`. `benchmarks/__tests__/guard-vocabulary-dispatch.test.ts` reads
all three files as text and asserts there is **no member literal anywhere in either routing branch, comment block
included**, that both halves forward rather than resolve, that no other occurrence of the flag pins a literal (the
seven golden branches are copies, so the seventh would have been invisible to a first-only check), and that both
CLIs keep the union as their only list.

**Nothing published moves**: the branch is read only when a dispatch names the key, and the default is the
engine's. What moves is reach — and the register's law about pins reads the same with the sign reversed. A pin
whose replacement is unreachable is still a pin; **a vocabulary whose seventh word is unreachable is still a
closed axis**, and it stays closed for a reason that is not the measurement.

### …and the axis it had kept closed is now ENROLLED, on three populations

The dispatch repair was the precondition, not the result. With the seventh word reachable on both halves, the arm 239
refused was measured on the two corpora this register judges with, under a criterion written before the last of the
three numbers was read (`docs/transient-guard-evidence.md` §13):

| population                        | `evidence-trimmed` |            `hump` | movement                   |
| --------------------------------- | -----------------: | ----------------: | -------------------------- |
| RCAEval, nine cells, 735          |      657 = 89.39 % | **659 = 89.66 %** | **+2**, no cell down       |
| FSE'26, 1 422, `Top@1`            |       869 = 61.1 % |  **874 = 61.5 %** | **+5**, one type down by 1 |
| RCABench TT archive, 1 303 paired |      750 = 57.56 % | **759 = 58.25 %** | **+9** (12 / 3)            |

**The guard row above is therefore closed a fourth and last time, and this time by enrolment rather than by refusal:**
`DEFAULT_TRANSIENT_GUARD_TEST = 'hump'`. Three populations, one sign, one regressed case on the golden half (paid for
inside its own cell and fault type) and one regressed type on FSE'26 (one case of 46). The transfer names itself:
`ContainerKill` is the largest single move in the arm (+2 of 89), which is the fault type the shape describes.

What the axis cost to close, in iterations: five arms measured (`level-window`, `either`, `evidence-aware`,
`trimmed-ends`, `hump`), two refusals of the last one, one mis-specified bar corrected rather than moved, and one
dispatch surface repaired so that the fourth reading could exist at all. **What it was never short of was numbers; it
was short of a place to put the seventh one.**

## Iteration 246 — an axis this register could not have listed, because the column was filed under a blank name

Every row above is an axis that was **measured and refused**. This one is the other kind, and it is recorded
because the register's whole purpose is to stop a re-derivation, and a re-derivation needs a place to start
from. The pod lifecycle — a container restart, a readiness drop, a phase change — was not closed. It was not
open. It was **invisible**, and the reason was a converter predicate: `service_name IS NOT NULL` was the rule
that dropped an unowned metric row, and the pod-scoped k8s channels put the **empty string** in that column.
Every datapack therefore carried one node named `''` holding forty-eight pod- and container-scoped gauges, and
no service's channel list contained any of them. `docs/pod-state-term.md` §2 records the repair.

The measurement that enrols it, on the whole archive — 1,422 datapacks scored in two waves of 711 with the
same configuration, combined on per-case results:

| population                 |      term absent | `podStateWeight = 8` | movement                                       |
| -------------------------- | ---------------: | -------------------: | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **FSE'26, 1,422, `Top@1`** | **873 = 61.39%** |   **1,066 = 74.96%** | **+193 cases, +13.57 pp**                      |
| FSE'26, 1,422, `Top@3`     |   1,136 = 79.89% |       1,225 = 86.15% | +89, +6.26 pp                                  |
| FSE'26, 1,422, `Top@5`     |   1,184 = 83.26% |       1,247 = 87.69% | +63, +4.43 pp                                  |
| `JVMMemoryStress`, 171     |       61 = 35.7% |     **171 = 100.0%** | +110                                           |
| `ContainerKill`, 89        |       27 = 30.3% |       **88 = 98.9%** | +61                                            |
| `PodFailure`, 24           |         1 = 4.2% |       **23 = 95.8%** | +22                                            |
| `PodKill`, 10              |        5 = 50.0% |            5 = 50.0% | **0** — the channels cannot read a deleted pod |
| the other 21 types, 1,128  |      779 = 69.1% |          779 = 69.1% | **0**                                          |

**Twenty-two of the twenty-five fault types are identical to the case.** That is the cost side, and it is
measured on the whole population rather than on a sample: a term with a specificity of 1.01 non-zero services
per datapack (§5 of its document) is a pointer rather than a coefficient, which is why the weight is 8 rather
than 1 and why the curve saturates there instead of climbing.

Two readings that are easy to get wrong and are recorded so they are not:

- **The baseline reads 873 against the register's 874.** The arm is at weight ZERO, so the one case cannot be
  the term; it is attributed to the converter's attribution change, which gives every service the pod-scoped
  channels it was silently missing and therefore moves the anomaly scores underneath. Both arms were measured
  in the same session, which is what makes the pair comparable.
- **`NetworkBandwidth` contains one fleet-wide restart event** — one of its 42 datapacks fires the term on 49
  services at once. It cost nothing (20/42 at both weights, because a uniform offset cannot re-order), but it
  names the next axis: a channel that moves across the fleet in one window should be discounted the way a
  shared metric is, and that is a gate rather than a smaller weight.

**What this row does NOT claim:** that a bigger weight is better. 8 and 16 are identical to the case, and the two
residual misses at saturation are pool admission, not weight — the pointer is right and its candidate never enters
the pool. Tuning this knob to chase them would be the "flippable vs would-be-hurt" mistake the top of this
register exists to prevent.

## Iteration 247 — the fault type the register's own row said the term could not read

The row above ends with a sentence that this iteration falsified: _"`PodKill` is flat at 50.0% at every weight
because a deleted pod stops reporting."_ A deleted pod does not stop reporting — a **new** one starts. What
stops is the _declaration's_ counters, and the three state channels read the declaration. The pod object's own
cumulative counters (`container.cpu.time`, `k8s.pod.cpu.time`, `k8s.pod.network.io`) restart at zero when the
object is replaced, which is a fourth kind of fact and now a fourth indicator:

| population              |         before |              after |
| ----------------------- | -------------: | -----------------: |
| `PodKill`, 10 datapacks |      5 = 50.0% |    **10 = 100.0%** |
| `PodFailure`, 24        |     23 = 95.8% |    **24 = 100.0%** |
| `ContainerKill`, 89     |     88 = 98.9% |    **89 = 100.0%** |
| FSE'26, 1,422, `Top@1`  | 1,066 = 74.96% | **1,073 = 75.46%** |

Two more mechanisms came out of the same pass, and one candidate mechanism was **measured and refused**:

- **A restart counter that was already non-zero is not an event.** Of the 146 restart increments across the
  archive's 145 first-wave lifecycle datapacks, 142 are on the truth starting from an untouched counter, one is
  on the truth starting from a non-zero one, and **all three** bystanders start from a non-zero one. Requiring
  `lastPre = 0` removed every bystander, cost one truth, and took `PodFailure` from 17/18 to 18/18.
- **Evidence covering the fleet is not about a service.** One datapack per wave fires on 49 of 50 services at
  once; `POD_STATE_MAX_FLEET_SHARE` refuses the reading when the firing set is more than half the candidates.
  Turning the gate off changes 1 of 711 ranked orders and not the top of either.
- **Pool admission was refused, on measurement.** The previous row predicted the two residual misses were a
  candidate that "never enters the pool". Widening the pool to admit non-zero pod-state evidence changed
  **0 of 1,422** ranked orders. It was reverted rather than shipped; the misses are a `log`-dominance loss
  (`ts2-mysql-pod-kill-xvzmxb`) and a chronic-restarter tie (`ts3-mysql-pod-failure-58qts5`), and the second
  one is now closed by the rule above.

## Iteration 252 — one guard whose denominator mixed two periods, and the first term measured PAST its own ceiling

Neither entry is a coefficient that was moved and refused. The first is a **correctness** repair to a guard this
register already leans on, and the second is the first term in the register's history whose pre-registered bound
was **beaten** and which is still refused — so the two numbers that close it are on opposite sides of the bar.

**The guard.** `duty-cycled-idle` drops a channel that sits near zero for more than 40% of its samples, and it
counted those samples over the **whole recording** — while the first half of every recording is the pre-injection
window, in which a fault's `error` channel is quiet _by construction_. The denominator mixed a period where zero
is the expected reading with a period where zero is information. On `RE3:SockShop` that refused the **truth's own
`error` channel on 18 of 30 cases and the winner's on none**, and the refuse/keep split is the proof rather than
the symptom:

| truth's `error` channel, `RE3:SockShop` | cases | rank-1 correct |      rate |
| --------------------------------------- | ----: | -------------: | --------: |
| refused (`duty-cycled-idle`)            |    18 |              8 | **44.4%** |
| kept                                    |    12 |             11 | **91.7%** |
| **winner's** channel refused            | **0** |              — |         — |

The window is now the post-injection slice for `EVENT_METRIC_LABELS = ['error']` — the one family whose zero is a
measured zero — and the corpus census over all 735 cases reads **39 channels admitted, 0 newly refused**. The
latency families were deliberately NOT windowed, and the same census is why: they would admit 20 of 39 and 25 of 38
there, which is a different axis than the one being repaired. What the change is worth on the published numbers is
one cell's secondary metric and nothing else:

| population                        |       before |        after | movement                                   |
| --------------------------------- | -----------: | -----------: | ------------------------------------------ |
| RCAEval, nine cells, `AC@1`       | 660 = 89.80% | 660 = 89.80% | **0 — no cell moves, in either direction** |
| `RE3:SockShop`, type-mean `Avg@5` |        84.6% |    **85.6%** | **+1.0 pp**                                |

**The term.** `docs/rcaeval-error-scale.md` §6 pre-registered a collision-source term over `Δλ` — the ABSOLUTE
change in a node's own per-request error rate, the only quantity in the fusion whose unit is a rate — with an upper
bound of **26/30** on `RE3:SockShop`, written before the code existed. Built (`emissionWeight`, floor `0.1`
errors/request, absent-not-zero on every refusal), swept, and it **beats the bound**: `19 → 28/30` at `w = 0.65`.
It ships at **0**, because the same weight that buys that cell costs four others:

| `RE3:SockShop` | `RE3:TrainTicket` | `RE3:OnlineBoutique` | `RE2:SockShop` |  total |
| -------------: | ----------------: | -------------------: | -------------: | -----: |
|    19 → **28** |       22 → **19** |          26 → **24** |    89 → **88** | **+3** |

Net `+3` with four cells down is the trade this register's law refuses, and `w = 0` is not a compromise: the term's
map is not even built, so the shipped order is byte-identical to the whole table above. `docs/emission-intensity.md`
carries the sweep, the floor's justification (`RE1:OnlineBoutique`'s largest change in any case is `0.0003`, so
`0.1` cannot make that cell noisy) and the refutation that was visible **before** any engine ran: on
`RE3:TrainTicket` the truth's own `Δλ` has `p90 = 0` while the case's largest is `0.96`, so the node emitting more
per request there is the service returning the bad value, not the source. **A term whose premise is false on one
cell and inverted on another cannot be priced globally**, and the axis it names next is a case-level conjunction of
`Δλ` with the direction evidence (`failedEdge` / `lat`) — which is why the term is retained as code rather than
deleted: the next arm is a gate on it, not a weight on it.

`docs/duty-cycle-window.md` holds the confound proof, the 735-case flip census and the nine cells; both documents
are registered here by name because a measurement a reader cannot find is a measurement that gets re-derived.

## Iteration 253 — a graph that named a service the metrics had never heard of, and the axis that needed the direction channel it could not find

Two entries, and neither is a coefficient. The first is a **name join** between two artefacts of one case; the
second **closes** the axis iteration 252 named next, by measuring the channel it required and finding it empty.

**The join.** A trace file and a `metrics.json` are two artefacts of the same deployment. On
`RE2:OnlineBoutique` the spans spell the front end `frontendservice` and the metrics spell it `frontend`, and
nothing joined them — so `augmentTopologyWithTraces`, whose rule is "no span, no edge", dropped all seven YAML
edges starting at `frontend` and installed four from a node with **no metrics**. The dump then reported a
`latRise` of `14.233` and one `latEdges` on that phantom while the node the cell actually ranks reported "no
latency evidence", on **89 of the cell's 90 cases** (every case but one; the count of phantom nodes over the
corpus is exactly 89, all here — RE3:OnlineBoutique, the same system, was unaffected because its trace files
spell the front end correctly). `traceServiceResolver` binds a span name to the case's own id in three ordered
rules — identity, then spelling after dropping punctuation and case, then the same after removing a trailing
`service` — and REFUSES a normalised spelling that two ids both claim, because attributing one node's spans to
another is the one error the join cannot repair downstream. It is applied once, in the corpus owner, and
handed to the two streaming passes that read `traces.csv` a second time for memory reasons.

What it is worth on the published numbers is **nothing**, and that is measured rather than assumed: **0 of 735
cases changed winner**, `660` before and after, every cell's `AC@1` and `Avg@5` identical. Two mechanisms
explain the null and both are properties of the shipped configuration: `latWeight` reads a callee's INBOUND
rise as a maximum over callers (the front end has no callers, and the maximum on that cell was already held by
`checkoutservice`/`recommendationservice`), while the outbound readers are `topoWeight` (shipped `0`) and the
failed-call channel (26 records in 23,105 node-reads). It ships anyway, because a term added tomorrow would
otherwise be priced against a graph where the front end of 90 cases had no edges — the first victim would have
been the measurement.

**The axis, closed.** `docs/emission-intensity.md` §5 named a case-level admission conjoining `Δλ` with the
direction evidence. Measured on the corpus: the failed-call ledger carries a record on **26 of 23,105
node-reads**, so a conjunction with it admits **0 of 735 cases** and the term would be inert everywhere. The
two admissions that CAN be computed — Newcombe's lower bound on the rate difference, and the excess over a
node's callees — both repair `RE3:TrainTicket` completely (`19 → 22`, the three cases have `Δλ` `0.104…0.125`
against bounds `0.074…0.091`) and both still cost `RE2:OB −1`, `RE2:SS −1`, `RE3:OB −2`: net `+6` with three
cells down, refused by the same law as the weight itself. The reason is not statistical: in all four lost cases
the truth **does not emit** — `0 / 13,217` and `0 / 710` errors per post-window requests on two, and **no
`error` channel at all** on the other two, because a `loss` fault makes the source silent and its callers
eloquent. No statistic of the emission channel can separate a source from a caller emitting on a dead
dependency's behalf; that is a DIRECTION question, and this corpus does not carry the direction channel it
needs. The term stays at `0`, the two admissions are recorded so nobody prices them twice, and the
prerequisite is named: `edgeRecords`, which is the one signal the FSE'26 separator census reports as holding
(AUC 0.908, 60–2, five folds), is where such a term would have to be measured.

`docs/span-name-join.md` holds the join's two-artefact table, the before/after graph, the nine cells and the
neutrality argument.

## Iteration 254 — the weight that could not ship, and the one inference that was doing the damage

The emission axis was closed twice: at its weight in iteration 252 (`+3` net, four cells down) and at its
admission in 253 (`+6` net, three cells down; the direction channel it asked for does not exist on this
corpus — 26 records in 23,105 node-reads). Both closures were arithmetically right and both were diagnosing the
wrong organ. The seven cases the arm lost share one property that neither record named: **the node the arm
overturned carries no emission entry at all** — two are silent (`0 / 13,217` and `0 / 710` post-window
requests), five have no `error` channel. `computeEmissionScores` is sparse by design and its absence means "this
case cannot answer for this node"; the additive term read that absence as a measured ZERO, and a zero share
loses to every node the term could measure.

The repair is an order rather than a coefficient: the term permutes the candidates it MEASURED and may not move
one across a candidate it could not measure (`orderWithEmissionJurisdiction`). Measured on the nine cells, three
arms from one tree:

| arm                               | RE1:OB | RE1:SS |  RE1:TT | RE2:OB | RE2:SS | RE2:TT | RE3:OB | RE3:SS | RE3:TT |   total |
| --------------------------------- | -----: | -----: | ------: | -----: | -----: | -----: | -----: | -----: | -----: | ------: |
| `w = 0`                           |    113 |    119 |     112 |     84 |     89 |     76 |     26 |     19 |     22 | **660** |
| `w = 0.5`, ungated                |    113 |    119 |     113 |     83 |     88 |     76 |     24 | **28** |     19 |     663 |
| `w = 0.5`, jurisdiction (SHIPPED) |    113 |    119 | **113** |     84 |     89 |     76 |     26 | **24** |     22 | **666** |

`+6` with **no cell down** — `RE1:TrainTicket +1`, `RE3:SockShop +5`, and all five cells the ungated arm moved
the wrong way return to their shipped values. Paired sign test `6–0`, `p = 0.0156`. The case-level replay of the
same rule (which prices exactly, because it only switches the term on or off) predicted `666` with the same two
cells moving before any engine ran. Sensitivity at `0.35 / 0.50 / 0.65`: `RE3:SS 22 / 24 / 24`, `RE1:TT 113 /
113 / 113` — monotone, flat above the pre-registered value, and no grid was searched.

Two things this closes rather than defers. **The intake hypothesis is refuted**: the first candidate for the
missing direction channel was the corpus's `workload`, on the kinetic reading that a source loses its intake
while a caller keeps its own — and on `RE3:SockShop` the winning source's intake ratio is `1.010`, `1.001`,
`0.977`, i.e. unchanged, because the source is the service nearest a dead dependency and it keeps answering
while failing. **And the four gains the rule forfeits are named rather than lost**: on `re3ss_carts_f4_2`,
`orders_f3_3`, `orders_f4_2`, `orders_f4_3` the shipped leader also carries no entry and the truth IS the
largest emitter — a direction gate would have taken them, and this corpus does not carry one.

`docs/emission-jurisdiction.md` holds the rule, the seven cases with their readings, the three arms, the
sensitivity table and the refutation; `docs/emission-intensity.md` §7 records that its own §6 refused the term
for the right observation and the wrong reason.

### The residual it leaves, mapped — and the next candidate refused before it was built

`666/735` leaves **69 misses**, and they are not spread evenly enough for "improve ranking" to be a plan:

By fault type:

| fault type                        | misses |
| --------------------------------- | -----: |
| `loss`                            | **35** |
| `delay`                           |     12 |
| `f4` (RE3)                        |      7 |
| `f3` (RE3)                        |      5 |
| `f1` (RE3)                        |      4 |
| `f2` (RE3)                        |      2 |
| `cpu` / `disk` / `mem` / `socket` | 1 each |

By cell:

| cell                 | correct | misses |
| -------------------- | ------: | -----: |
| `RE1:OnlineBoutique` | 113/125 |     12 |
| `RE1:SockShop`       | 119/125 |      6 |
| `RE1:TrainTicket`    | 113/125 |     12 |
| `RE2:OnlineBoutique` |   84/90 |      6 |
| `RE2:SockShop`       |   89/90 |      1 |
| `RE2:TrainTicket`    |   76/90 |     14 |
| `RE3:OnlineBoutique` |   26/30 |      4 |
| `RE3:SockShop`       |   24/30 |      6 |
| `RE3:TrainTicket`    |   22/30 |      8 |

Half the residual is one fault type, and **37 of the 69 are a one-hop NEIGHBOUR of the truth** — 25 where the
winner is a direct caller, 12 where it is a callee, 32 unrelated. That is a direction signature, and the census
says where the advantage sits: over the 33 `loss` misses that carry a full term breakdown, the winner's margin
is `selfAnomalyLog1p` `0.657` against the truth's `0.448` (`+0.209`) and `dualFamily` `0.121` against `0.023`
(`+0.098`), with **every other term at `0.000`** — the weights are zero or the inputs are absent.

So the next candidate had to be direction, and it was priced from the shipped dumps before any code existed, with
the engine's own `prediction=` order as the control — it must reproduce the battery, or the probe is measuring
the probe:

| rule applied to the engine's own order                                               |   total | reordered | won | lost |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------: | --------: | --: | ---: |
| engine order (control)                                                               | **666** |         — |   — |    — |
| a caller may not outrank a called dependency whose `selfAnomaly` is at least its own |     665 |       179 |   1 |    2 |
| a node may not outrank a dependency whose onset precedes its own by ≥ `0` ms         |     591 |       272 |   6 |   81 |
| … ≥ `1,000` ms                                                                       |     603 |       269 |   6 |   69 |
| … ≥ `5,000` ms                                                                       |     613 |       256 |   6 |   59 |
| … ≥ `10,000` ms                                                                      |     617 |       231 |   3 |   52 |

**Both refused, and for stated reasons.** Magnitude is IMPORTED, not authored: a caller's anomaly is its callee's
plus its own, so "equally anomalous dependency" fires on healthy aggregators — `ts-order-service`, `carts` and
`checkoutservice` lose their own cases to `carts-db`, `ts-seat-service` and `paymentservice`, which is the same
error the rule was meant to repair, mirrored. Onset is a DETECTION BUCKET, not a propagation time: leaf
datastores flip their bucket first because they have one metric family, so the rule demotes sources wholesale.
Neither is a direction channel, and no threshold rescues either — the best lag still loses `49`.

Recorded so the axis is not re-attempted from per-node data: **on this corpus, direction is not expressible from
any per-node statistic the export carries.** It needs an edge-level one, which RCAEval does not ship (`0`
failed-edge latency records over 125 cases) and the FSE'26 half does (`docs/fse26-separator-verdict.md`:
`edgeRecords`, AUC `0.908`, `60–2`).

## Iteration 255 — four ways an absent lookup was answered with a value

The 254th iteration's defect was "a sparse map's absence was read as a measured zero". This iteration asked
what else answers a question the caller was never asked, and found three more, in the one public API that had
no caller to notice them. `docs/engine-input-contracts.md` carries the whole audit, and `docs/production-leave-one-out.md` carries the
accounting that audit made possible (three counterfactuals where the battery had one, and the discovery that
`RE1`'s score lives entirely in weights no flag can reach); the axis itself is recorded here because it closes a
SEARCH direction, not a single line of code:

- **Do not guess an input contract, and do not guard it three ways.** `TreeRCAEngine.analyze` enforced
  "endpoints are nodes" as two silent skips plus one unguarded write, and the unguarded one crashed the engine
  inside `topologicalSort` with a message about `.length`. Three inconsistent defaults is worse than none: they
  disagree with each other, and the disagreement is not visible from any of them.
- **A validation helper that cannot see `NaN` is not a validation helper.** `invariantRange` was used 38 times
  and `NaN` passed every one; `topo-deduction.ts` had already worked around it locally, which is the signature
  of a tool that is wrong rather than a caller that is careful.
- **A record is not an edge.** A repeated `(from, to)` pair was worth `+0.033` on the parent's score
  (`0.528` against `0.495`) whenever the cap did not mask it — the cap masked it on every shipped corpus,
  which is why "it never happened" was true and "it cannot happen" was not.
- **`!` on a map read is a promise the compiler does not keep.** Four of them turned a missing edge into `NaN`,
  and only the range check downstream was in a position to see it — with no idea which edge.

None of these moves `666/735`, and the register states why rather than assuming it: the three topologies carry
121 unique edges, a dangling endpoint would have crashed the previous battery, a `NaN` score would have printed
as a `NaN` confidence, and `analyze` is not on the benchmark path. The last point is the one worth keeping: a
public API with no production caller is where defects go to survive a green CI, so the contracts are now
asserted by 15 tests that never touch the battery's own arithmetic.

## Iteration 256 — the vector, priced; and the arm that gains

The 255th iteration ended with an accounting that had one measured column and one prose column, and named the
arms that would close it. This iteration ran them: ten single-coefficient removals on the configuration behind
`666/735`, one per suite, with the shipped configuration as the control row. `docs/production-weight-leave-one-out.md`
carries the table; the axis is recorded here because it closes the last claim the register has been carrying
without a number — _what each shipped term is worth_ — and because two of its findings are directions rather than
measurements:

- **Five of the ten coefficients move no case at all**, and the artifact's own verdict block separates the two
  reasons. `latWeight` — the largest weight in the vector — is `STARVED` on `RE1` and both SockShop packs (those
  corpora carry no spans) and `INERT` where it has an input; the pool penalty, the stability prior and the
  failed-edge term are `INERT` on every cell. **A `0.0` from a starved channel is a statement about the corpus**,
  and the register now says which of the five zeros are which.
- **`anomalyCvWeight = 0.05` costs two cases** (`RE2:TrainTicket`, `RE3:TrainTicket`) and buys none: `LESS CV`
  reads `668/735`, the only arm in the study that gains — and the arm survives the instrument that publishes. The
  golden runner at `anomaly_knobs=cv=0` (`42666007350`) reads `345 / 250 / 73`, i.e. the same two cells and
  nothing else, so the reading is not an artefact of the ablation's own corpus assembly. **The default is not
  changed here**: the criterion is an AND over both halves and the coefficient is live on FSE'26, which is why the
  change is pre-registered rather than taken. `LESS TREND` reads the same `RE3` case back and loses
  two elsewhere, so it is refused — the two shares are not symmetric and the reason is that dispersion is not
  evidence of a fault shape while monotone drift is. The joint arm (`TREND + CV OFF`) is **pre-registered, not
  run**, because the two single arms landing on the same case count is consistent with one shared mechanism and
  with two independent cases, and choosing between those readings after seeing the gain is the fitting this
  register has refused three times.
- **`podStateWeight = 8` cannot be priced here**, and the register records the reason the docblock on the
  exemption already gave, now checked: no metric family in the corpus is a pod lifecycle reading. The term is
  priced on FSE'26 (`docs/pod-state-term.md`) and is `0` on this half by construction, not by measurement.

One defect was found by building the instrument rather than by running it: `run-ablation.ts` measures every Δ from
`allRuns[0]`, so a selection that began at an arm reported ten numbers against an arm — visible in the verdict
block as `varies=selfAnomalyWeight,<own field>` on every row. The selection now carries its control explicitly
(`PRODUCTION_WEIGHT_CONFIGS`), and the fence asserts the control is the shipped configuration. The same fence
holds the partition: a weight that ships non-zero and has neither an arm nor a stated reason fails the build.

## Iteration 257 — the shares are one composite, and the half that could not be measured

Two things happened, and the second is the larger one.

**The pre-registered joint arm refutes the additive reading of the anomaly composition.** `TREND` and `CV` were
the only pair whose single arms landed on the same case with opposite signs; the question was written down before
the arms existed (`667` = one shared case, `668` = two independent cases) and neither number is what the pair
reads. `LESS TREND + CV` is **`665/735`**: `RE1` `345`, `RE2` **`247`**, `RE3` `73`, against a sum of singles that
predicts `667` and a measured interaction of `−2`. The witnesses are fault-type cells, not prose: `RE1` SockShop
`loss` gains a case **only** when both shares are gone (`19/19/19 → 20`), `RE2` OnlineBoutique `loss` loses a
second case the singles never touched (`12/11/12 → 10`), and `RE3` TrainTicket `f2` is recovered by either
removal alone (`5/6/6 → 6`), i.e. one case, not two. The mechanism is in the code rather than inferred: the shares
are additive in `featureScore`, and the interaction arrives when `buildTopologyFaultGraph` **re-scales the field
over the fleet** — a share moves the maximum, so it moves every candidate's base term, and only then is the
result compared against the weighted signals. **`anomalyCvWeight = 0` is therefore not shipped** despite its
`+2`: the same corpus moves to `665` under one adjacent edit, so the margin is a knife edge, and the register's
rule about summaries outliving corrections applies to a default change exactly as it applies to a sentence.

**And the second half of the kill criterion was, until this iteration, measuring a corpus the engine could not
read.** A dispatch at `74e1a306` was refused outright: `converterDigest mismatch: cache sha256:f83af14d…,
checkout sha256:f72899e5…`. The cache the consumer defaults to (`rcabench-latency-full`) was built **2026-09-14**;
the converter gained the pod-lifecycle channel on **2026-11-08** (`cc26232d`), which `podStateWeight = 8` reads. So
the published `61.46% (874/1422)` is a reading of shards on which that term's map was **empty by construction**,
and no dispatch could produce a different one. The cache was rebuilt through its own documented path
(`rcabench-data` run `42721719446`, tag `rcabench-pod-v1`, converter digest equal to this checkout's) and the pair
re-run at `4d0050d7`:

| run           | knobs                 |      Top@1 |     cases |
| ------------- | --------------------- | ---------: | --------: |
| `42729721072` | shipped               | **75.46%** | 1073/1422 |
| `42729735767` | `anomaly_cv_weight=0` | **75.46%** | 1073/1422 |

**The aggregate is byte-identical and the criterion still fails**, which is the finding worth keeping: the two runs
differ on **four fault types** — `JVMException` 30→31 and `HTTPRequestReplacePath` 38→39 up, `HTTPRequestDelay`
57→56 and `PodKill` 10→9 **down**. `+2` and `−2` are the same total and not the same result, and the rule this
project applies to every candidate is _zero regressed fault types_, so **`anomalyCvWeight = 0` is refused on the
criterion itself**, not merely on the knife-edge argument above. A 1422-case aggregate that hides a two-for-two
swap is exactly the class of summary this register exists to keep out of a decision.

The `61.46% → 75.46%` move is a **corpus** change and is recorded as one in `docs/sota-comparison.md`: the engine
did not improve, the evidence it can see did, and which converter change produced the 199 cases is unmeasured.

The register records all three because they are the same failure in three costumes — a number whose provenance was
one step weaker than the sentence it supported — and because the third one is the reason this iteration ends with
no default changed: the criterion was satisfiable after all, and the answer it gave was _no_.

## Iteration 258 — the corpus move is one term; and two things that decided a number were not the number

**The 199 cases iteration 257 could not attribute are the pod-state term, and the arithmetic closes.** The
question was written as a complement before it was run: switch the term off on the same cache at the same commit
and see whether the published score falls back to the pre-rebuild reading. It does.
`ranking_knobs=pod_state_weight=0` (`42736219773`, cache `rcabench-pod-v1`, digest `f72899e5…`, commit
`59cd1ad3`) reads **`873/1422 = 61.39%`** against the shipped **`1073/1422 = 75.46%`** (`42729721072`), and the
two runs' 49-field `config` blocks differ in **one field**. Four fault types move — `JVMMemoryStress` `171→61`,
`ContainerKill` `89→27`, `PodFailure` `24→1`, `PodKill` `10→5`, `−200` in total — and **twenty-one do not move at
all**. So `874 (old corpus) ≈ 873 (new corpus, term off)`: the corpus change is that one term, and the engine's
own contribution to the move is **one case, in the wrong direction**. `75.46%` keeps its meaning ("the engine on
evidence it can now see") and loses the meaning it never had ("the engine improved"). `docs/pod-state-term.md`
§11 carries the four-type table and the Top@3/Top@5 shifts (`86.29 → 79.89`, `87.83 → 83.26`), which say the term
moves RANKS and not only the top one.

The caveat was stated rather than smoothed — **type-level zero is not case-level zero** — and then measured
instead of left standing. The same day's dispatches published the verdict artefact, and the case level reads
**`gained 0, lost 200`** at Top@1 and `gained 0, lost 91` at Top@3, with **every one of the twenty-one
untouched types at exactly `0/0`**. The term moves the Top-1 answer on 200 of 1422 cases and on all 200 the
movement is the verdict's: no case changed its answer without changing from wrong to right. The type table and
the case table agree, which is the first time this repository has been able to say that about a term rather than
about a summary.

**`js/regex-injection` `#14` is closed as FIXED, not dismissed.** Two suppression spellings had been carried on
the sink for several iterations (`codeql[rule-id]` above it, `lgtm[rule-id]` on it), and the register's own rule
— _a comment is not a fix_ — applied to them the whole time: `#13` stayed open for a fortnight and adding the
second spelling only relocated the alert. The sink was `new RegExp(commandLine)`, and the honest removal is to
stop constructing a regular expression from a command line at all. `--family` now takes a **glob** compiled into
a predicate (`compileFamilyGlob`): `*` is the only metacharacter, every other character is literal, and matching
is a left-to-right search for the pattern's literal segments — which is exactly what an unanchored `test` meant.
Two behaviours change and both are corrections: `db.*` no longer matches `dbx` (a dot is a dot), and there is no
malformed-pattern throw because a glob has no malformed form — replaced by two refusals that a filter cannot have
and a family must not: the empty pattern, and a pattern made only of wildcards. The `lastIndex` invariant the old
matcher neutralised is now structural (a predicate closing over its segments has no state), and its test is kept
as a COUNT because the count is what broke, not the mechanism that fixed it.

**The FSE'26 cache was selected by a human-maintained tag, and the tag went stale in the one way that costs a
run.** `shard_tag` defaulted to `rcabench-latency-full`, whose manifest records converter `f83af14d…`; this
checkout computes `f72899e5…` since `cc26232d`. For one iteration **every bare dispatch was refused by the
workflow's own provenance gate**, and the refusal named two digests and no tag, so the operator's next step was
to download eight release manifests by hand. The identification of a cache is its digest — the field the gate
already checks — so the tag is now **discovered from it**: `fse26_cache_select.py` takes this checkout's digest
and the set of released caches, and refuses on both sides (zero matches = rebuild; two matches = pin, because a
name must not decide). `shard_tag` is still accepted as an explicit override and is still gate-checked. The
inventory this produced is recorded in `docs/fse26-cache-selection.md`, including the two tags that share
`f83af14d…` (`rcabench-prefix-latency` and `rcabench-latency-full`) — which is the ambiguity branch of the
selector, measured rather than imagined, and the reason it refuses rather than picks.

**The per-case verdicts are published, and the census is what caught it.** `run-fse26.ts` has taken
`--per-case-out` since the judgement question came up and no workflow ever passed it; the census listed it as an
operational flag no workflow reaches, with the reason _"the ranking it exports is the one the run already
counted"_. That reason is the same mistake the joint arm punished one iteration earlier — a fault type's **count**
cannot distinguish `+2/−0` from `+2/−2` — so the flag is now passed, the file is uploaded with the other two, and
`scripts/compare_fse26_per_case.py` reads two runs as cases — `docs/fse26-per-case-verdicts.md` —: gained, lost, corpus differences excluded (a corpus
difference is not a flip), and a `NET-ZERO BUT NOT IDENTICAL` section for every type whose count is unchanged and
whose case set is not. The push that wired the flag failed `Release` on `dispatch-surface-census`, which is the
census doing its job in the direction it was built for; the entry was **removed**, not reworded, because that
list only moves by removal when a flag becomes reachable. Correctness is recomputed from each row's own
`accepted`/`ranked`, so `--depth` re-judges Top@1 as Top@3 over the same bytes.

**And the most-read line of `docs/sota-comparison.md` was anchored to a panel that cannot read telemetry.** The
FSE'26 STANDING row printed `+38.5 pp over the best 37%` — arithmetic against the benchmark paper's own panel
(avg 21%, best 37%, `arXiv:2510.04711`) — while the 2026 agent literature on the same benchmark reports up to
**90.0%** (Sonnet·ThinkDepth.ai, `arXiv:2608.21310` Table 2). The document said _"we are not first on RCABench"_
three sections later, so nothing in it was false; the row was, by omission, and the row is what gets quoted. It
now prints both anchors, the position this corpus holds (**4th** in the agentic panel, `−14.5 pp` behind the
best, `−28.5 pp` on the pre-rebuild corpus), and it names the panel in the cell rather than in a footnote. The
2026-11-10 sweep found **no new entrant**: `2610.35767` (RCAtlas), `2611.02416` (SLM RCA) and `2609.27069`
(graph-vs-flat) are each already in the record with their own caveats, so the sweep's only change is this row.

## Iteration 259 — the guard reached one corpus, the error channel is thrown away on the other, and completing it is refused

**A repair that is correct, tested, documented — and unreachable where the score is measured.** Iteration 78
found that the idle guard's denominator is the whole recording, and that a fault case's first half is quiet BY
CONSTRUCTION, so the 40 % line sat below the structural floor of any channel a fault moves; the repair measures
an EVENT channel over the post-injection half instead. Event membership is an exact list of literal labels
(`EVENT_METRIC_LABELS`), written against the RCAEval converter's name for that channel, `error`. The FSE'26
converter derives the same quantity from the same spans and calls it `http.response.error_rate`. It was never in
the list, so on the archive where `1073/1422` is measured the guard kept the whole-recording denominator and
dropped the truth's own error channel as `duty-cycled-idle`.

The dump, not a hypothesis: `ts2-ts-ui-dashboard-response-replace-code-7nldtm`, truth `ts-ui-dashboard`, whose
rate series reads `0.00` for 24 samples then `16.1 / 16.7 / 16.9 / …` while every decoy reads `0.00` throughout.
The same dump prints the family in `metricDrop(30): … duty-cycled-idle` AND as the node's decisive signal, and
the engine's prediction for that case does not contain the truth in its top five.

**Population** (`scripts/fse26_duty_cycle_sweep.py`, both windows replayed on every case's own truth channel):
of **1347** judgeable datapacks (1422 total, 74 whose truth service carries no rate series at all, 1 too short)
the whole-recording rule drops the truth's channel on **1344 — 99.8 %** — and the post-injection window keeps
**661**. The defect is enormous, and one label closes it.

**And one label is refused.** Measured at `31971bf1` on cache `rcabench-pod-v1`, per-case verdicts against the
shipped `59cd1ad3`: `Top@1 1073 → 1082`, `Top@3 86.29 → 87.90`, `Top@5 87.83 → 90.51` — with **eight fault
types moving, six up and four down** (`HTTPResponseReplaceCode +9`, `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod +4`,
`HTTPResponseAbort +2`, `HTTPResponseReplaceBody +1`, `JVMException +1`, `NetworkCorrupt +1` against
`NetworkPartition −4`, `NetworkBandwidth −3`, `HTTPRequestReplacePath −1`, `NetworkLoss −1`). That is a trade,
and this register's rule for every candidate — no regressed fault type, stated for `cv=0`, for the `pre-injection`
anchor and for the trend weight — has no exception for an arm whose total rises. The family therefore stays out
of the list, and the absence is written down as a **NAMED exemption with its number and its falsifier**
(`event-family-census.test.ts`) rather than left as the oversight it was.

**The mechanism is not the one that was predicted, and saying so is the point.** The 14 lost cases are not the
fleet-share shape the pod term abstains on — the affected fleet reads 23–38 %, under that gate. The truth in
eight of them is a service that **cannot produce the channel at all** (`mysql` has no HTTP spans) while its
callers can, so during a network fault on `mysql` the callers' error rise is priced as evidence _for the
callers_. The other six are a sibling swap (`ts-route-plan-service` losing to `ts-travel-plan-service` by one
rank). The engine ships `victimWeight = 0`, so the completion is a **victim/source asymmetry**, and the
acceptance test that would admit the label is pre-registered and falsifiable: `Top@1 >= 1082` **with no fault
type down**, on this cache, measured per case.

**Three papers entered the record without entering the leaderboard.** `arXiv:2609.23301` (TempoTrace) proves
NTP-grade clocks invert causality on **25–30 %** of directed operation pairs — the shipped `latWeight`
multiplies a latency measured from exactly those two stamps, and the propagation-τ axis is an estimate of a time
difference, so a τ fitted from traces is bounded by the clock. `arXiv:2609.27538` (Backstitch) measures silent
request-context breaks in **673 of 1133** production services — the graph is augmented from the case's own spans,
so an edge that drops context is an edge augmentation cannot see. `arXiv:2611.04769` (RESTberus) reports that
stock Train Ticket wires Hystrix circuit breakers which turn a downstream failure into an **empty payload or an
`HTTP 200 OK`**, so the boundary never reports it; the authors disable the fallbacks to make failures
observable, and their threats-to-validity admits that doing so exposes more than a production deployment would.
That last one lands on this project's own record: of the five cases `docs/emission-jurisdiction.md` §1 lists as
"no `error` channel at all", **two are `RE3:TrainTicket` `ts-route-service`** — the _wrong value_ axis, a
corrupted-payload fault whose caller sees `200`. Consistent, not proof, and the test that would settle it is
named (`docs/sota-populations.md`). None of the three is a competitor; all three bound a premise.

**What the iteration leaves behind that outlives its verdict:** a replay tool that prices the guard on any
corpus (`scripts/fse26_duty_cycle_sweep.py`, 28 tests, 100 % branch), a census that makes a producer's error
family impossible to forget (`event-family-census.test.ts`), and a refusal with a number and a falsifier instead
of a preference.

## Iteration 260 — the mechanism was not the predicate, and the gate cannot charge the winner

Iteration 259 wrote the fourteen lost datapacks of the second-spelling arm down as a victim/source asymmetry and
pre-registered the mechanism that would admit the label: the caller's error rise is priced as evidence for the
caller because the truth (`mysql`) cannot emit the channel at all. The next step was to make the caller
**chargeable**, and the first reading of the code said the reason it was not is a second copy of the event family
inside `isResponseChannel` — a literal `lower === 'error'` beside an `isEventMetric` that had been taught the
FSE'26 spelling.

**That defect is real and is fixed.** `isResponseChannel` is now expressed over the family
(`isResponseChannel(label, eventLabels?)`), the family travels as `eventExtraLabels` from the CLI through
`TopologyFaultGraphConfig` and is resolved **once** per pruner so the idle guard, the emission term and the
response predicate cannot disagree, and `__tests__/causal/event-family-admission.test.ts` asserts the relation
for every member — the assertion the literal would have failed. At the shipped family the change is inert by
construction: `lower === 'error'` became `EVENT_METRIC_LABEL_SET.has(lower)` on a set built from that
one-element array.

**It is not the mechanism, and the arm says so.** With the predicate agreeing, the eight `mysql`-truth datapacks
still read **0/8** — the refused arm's own answer. `ts2-mysql-bandwidth-jlzd96` is why: the accepted pair is
`[mysql, ts-config-service]`, the arm's rank 1 is `ts-seat-service` at anomaly `1.000` against the truth's
`0.939`, and `ts-seat-service` is the truth's **caller** (`ts-seat-service > ts-config-service > mysql`). The
term asks the right question of the right pair and the gate refuses the answer, because

```
charged(v) ⟺ min(a(v), e(v)) >= gate × a(v),   gate = 1  ⟺  e(v) >= a(v)
```

and for the **argmax** `a(c) <= a(v)` over every callee, so `e(v) <= a(v)` — the condition holds only on a tie.
**At the shipped gate the operator cannot charge the highest-anomaly node at all**, which is the only node a
ranking has to get right.

**And the term was additionally blind on this corpus.** `isLatencyMetric` is `startsWith('latency')`; the
FSE'26 converter writes `http.server.request.duration.max` and its mesh `hubble_http_request_duration_p50_seconds`,
so the caller-side predicate was false for nearly every node and `topoDiscount` did nothing on 1422 datapacks.
Widening it was built and **refused on measurement**: Top@1 on the eight datapacks falls **8/8 → 6/8**
(`NetworkPartition −1`, `NetworkBandwidth −1`), and `gate=0.5` recovers only one of the two (7/8, still a loss);
