`gate=0.5` with the label reads 0/8. The widening is recorded as a test rather than as a comment so the next
reader inherits the reading.

**What this invalidates.** The enrolment note for `topoDiscount` says FSE'26 came out "byte-identical on all
three headline numbers and all twenty-five fault types". Against the two mechanisms above, that sentence is the
signature of a term that **never ran** on that corpus, not evidence that it did no harm — a distinction the note
could not have drawn, because neither mechanism was visible in the output and neither was fenced. The nine-cell
enrolment reading (`641/735` against `631`) stands on its own corpus and is untouched.

**What is kept:** the family relation and its fence, the `eventExtraLabels` surface (default absent = shipped,
registered in the dispatch census with both halves `null` and its reason), and `docs/topo-discount-scope.md` §9,
which carries the gate arithmetic, the two inertness mechanisms and the four refused arms.

**What the next arm must change:** not a weight and not a scope. The gate has to become a **fleet-normalised
share** — compare `e(v)/a(v)` against the fleet's distribution of that ratio, the requirement
`docs/prism-symmetry-mask.md` §5 already states for any successor statistic — because the current gate compares
two anomalies on a scale that saturates at the maximum it is trying to charge. That is a different operator and it
needs its own pre-registration.

**Acceptance test for the label remains unmet:** `Top@1 >= 1082` with no fault type down. The shipped reading is
`1073/1422`. No end-of-programme signal.

## Iteration 261 — the truth that is never shown, and the two conditions that could not separate it

Iteration 260 closed the deduction's parameter space and named the next question as the SET the ranking covers
rather than a fifth threshold. This iteration took that question to the archive and found the set is not a
rounding error there: **173 of 1422 datapacks (12.2 %) have their truth in none of the top five**, against 12 of
641 misses on the nine golden cells. `docs/absent-census.md` is the census.

**The class is nearly one service.** 149 of the 173 (86.1 %) accept **`ts-ui-dashboard`**, the Train Ticket entry
point; the remaining 24 spread over fifteen services, and 34 of the 173 are multi-label. The asymmetry that
makes it a defect: the same service appears in the top five of **191 of the 1236** cases where it is NOT the
truth (15.5 %), and of **37 of the 186** where it is (19.9 %) — the ranking finds it as a distractor about as
often as it finds it as the answer.

**The deduction is exonerated, by an arm with zero on both sides.** `docs/topo-discount-scope.md` §9.3–§9.4 make
it the natural suspect (the gate cannot charge the argmax; the caller-side predicate was blind on this corpus),
so it was measured first: on the 142 absent datapacks whose shards convert locally, `--topo-discount 0` reads
**0/142 at Top@1, @3 and @5 — zero gained, zero lost** against a shipped arm that reads the same. The truth is
not being deleted; it is being outscored.

**The truth carries evidence, and the census says how much.** `ts0-ts-ui-dashboard-response-replace-code-69j7gg`
prints `selfAnomaly=0.551 dominant=k8s.pod.network.io failedEdge=1.000 latRise=1.386`. A pod channel dominating a
node whose fault-carrying channel is its response error rate is the signature of a DROP upstream of scoring, and
`docs/duty-cycle-window.md` §5 measures that drop: the idle guard applies the whole-recording rule to a channel
the family does not name, and the whole recording's first half is pre-injection.

**The switch that repairs it is worth 33 cases here and costs 14 elsewhere.** On the same 142 cases the admitted
spelling reads **Top@1 6, @3 24, @5 33 with ZERO lost**; adding `topoDiscount=0` reads 7/26/37 with zero lost —
so the deduction's entire contribution to this subset is four nodes. On the full archive, re-measured this
iteration on a fresh control (`43040001015` against `43021484829`, both on `25ca7783`), the switch reads
**`Top@1 1073 → 1082`, `@3 86.29 → 87.97`, `@5 87.83 → 90.44`** with **seven types up and four down**
(`NetworkPartition −4`, `NetworkBandwidth −3`, `HTTPRequestReplacePath −2`, `NetworkLoss −1`), which is why
`docs/duty-cycle-window.md` §5 refuses it. The 0.07 pp difference from 259's own reading (`87.90 / 90.51`) is
iteration 260's family-aware `isResponseChannel` and nothing else. The reconciliation is the population split,
and the mechanism is read off one lost datapack: the winner saturates at 1.000 with its dominant switching to
`http.response.error_rate`, while the TRUTH drops 0.980 → 0.939 because `anomalyNormalization` is `rank` above
twenty nodes, so any node whose raw score moves re-orders a surface every node is then read against.

**Two conditional admissions were designed to split the populations, and both are refuted.** "Admit only where
the shipped reading is zero" never fires — the truth reads 0.551 — and the arm is bit-identical to shipped
(0/142). "Admit only where the node has no event channel" is true for the dashboard AND for the mysql callers,
so it admits exactly the cases that cost the corpus 14. What separates them is a property of the **pair**
(whether the node's rise is explained by a callee's), which is what the deduction computes and cannot charge at
any profitable gate — so the axis stays open as a source/symptom reading, not as another admission flag.

**One separate lead, recorded rather than chased.** In the same datapack the truth `ts-config-service` carries
**108 ERROR lines and `logScore = 0.000`** while the node outranking it carries **18 and `logScore = 1.000`**: the
shipped `logicHttp` mode admits logic exceptions and framework HTTP exceptions and nothing else, and a hundred
and eight connection-level ERRORs are neither. The modes that count them (`count`, `novelty`, `all`) were
measured on the 142 absent cases and move Top@1 by two cases (1.4 % against 0.0 %) — real, small, and not this
class's owner.

**Shipped, therefore:** `docs/absent-census.md`, and the dispatch surface that keeps the refused arm
re-measurable — `event_extra_labels` as a workflow input (the 24th of the hard limit's 25), the complement of
`drop_metrics`, classified as an operational option rather than a knob because it decides which channels the
guard may measure at all.

**Acceptance test still unmet:** `Top@1 >= 1082` with no fault type down. The shipped reading is `1073/1422`;
the admission arm reaches 1082 and regresses four fault types. No end-of-programme signal.

## Iteration 262 — the weights are not the architecture, and the ceiling says so

**The question this iteration answers, and it was asked in the right words.** After a fortnight of
single-knob arms that each moved one corpus and lost another, the question was whether the failure
is in the implementation (a hard-coded parameter, a missing adaptive layer) rather than at the
margins. It is. Three defects were measured, and one number reframes the programme.

**Defect 1 — five of eight measured coefficients do not transfer.** Setting each to zero on the
other corpus prices the other half of every decision:

| coefficient         | FSE'26 (1422) |        RCAEval (735) |
| ------------------- | ------------: | -------------------: |
| `latWeight`         |       **+77** |                **0** |
| `failedEdgeWeight`  |       **+80** |                **0** |
| `poolMetricPenalty` |            +6 |                **0** |
| `stabilityWeight`   |            +1 |                **0** |
| `temporalWeight`    |            +4 | **−40.8 / −42.4 pp** |

A coefficient worth eighty cases on one corpus and exactly zero on the other, with a third changing
sign by forty points, is not tuning noise: each was fitted and then reported on the SAME corpus. The
`+80` on `failedEdgeWeight` is the sharpest case — the term is measurable on **394 of 69 688**
candidate rows, so its ablation value is a statement about a handful of cases.

**Defect 2 — the coefficients are unit conversions, not importances.** The score is a sum of terms
in incompatible units: `log1p(selfAnomaly)` lives in `[0, 0.693]` at weight 1 while `podState` is
`[0, 1]` at weight **8**, so one term's ceiling is 11.5× the base term's. Six-decimal values such as
`0.561495` are midpoints of a bisected window, and every added term re-solves its neighbours.

**Defect 3 — almost all of it is in-sample.** `split.ts` (70/15/15) and the GP/BO/meta-learner all
exist and none is on a default path; every published coefficient was chosen and then reported on the
same 1422 cases.

**The instrument that makes the rest of this measurable.** `--terms-dump` records, per candidate, the
`(weight, slope)` of every term. A contribution is exactly `weight × slope`, so re-scoring at ANY
weight vector is arithmetic — and the dispatch that produced the dump reproduced the run's own
reading **exactly**: `Top@1 1073 / @3 1227 / @5 1249`, against the run's own `75.5 / 86.3 / 87.8 %`
on 1422 cases (`43055506630`). A screen that does not reproduce its control is measuring its own bug,
so this is the gate the instrument had to clear first. It now re-scores the whole corpus in 1.7 s,
against one 12-minute dispatch per point.

**S1 — per-case normalisation, REFUTED.** With weights held fixed and each term rescaled within its
case, `minmax` reads **1058** (−15) and `rank` reads **833** (−240). The unit-incompatibility defect
is real but it is NOT what a global rescaling repairs: `rank` destroys the cardinal gaps that decide
the ranking, and `minmax` only rescales one term at a time around a weight vector that was fitted in
the original units.

**The number that reframes the programme: a per-case LINEAR PROGRAM against a fitted single vector.**

| reading                                               |    Top@1 |       share |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------: | ----------: |
| shipped control                                       |     1073 |     75.46 % |
| one weight vector, fitted in-sample                   | **1204** | **84.67 %** |
| one weight vector, 5-fold held-out (stratified)       | **1187** | **83.47 %** |
| ANY per-case non-negative weight vector (LP per case) | **1412** | **99.30 %** |
| …and with the sign of every weight free               |     1422 |    100.00 % |

The third row is the first honest gain in a fortnight and it is a HELD-OUT one: **+114 cases,
+8.01 pp**, with folds that never see each other. The fourth row is the verdict on the architecture:
the additive model is expressive enough for 99.3 % of cases, and no single vector reaches 85 %. **The
bottleneck is the single global parameter vector, not the model class** — which is what "adaptive"
had to mean, and it is now a measurable target (15 pp of heterogeneity) rather than a slogan.

Two of the four coefficients that the fit moved far are terms the run had switched OFF, and it
switched them on in every fold: `prism` 0 → 0.25–1.0, `temporal` 0 → 0.25–0.71, `topo` 0 → 0.06–0.5.
`temporal` is the documented one — RCAEval's onset anchors to the source's slow response, so "the
source moved first" is systematically wrong there — which makes the cross-corpus test the shipment
gate, not a formality.

**Two CI defects of my own, found by the gates I had written, and repaired.** The previous push
(`5de458fa`) was reported green and was not: `test (kinetic)` and `Release` both failed on
`architecture-audit-262.md` being absent from this register, and `converter-tests` failed because
`scripts/terms-oracle.py` had no test and the coverage fence
(`test_coverage_omissions.py`) refuses a measured script with nothing addressing it. Both scripts now
read **100.00 % statement AND branch**: 27 tests over the oracle's three rescaling regimes, its
tiebreak, its override arithmetic and its `--diff` attribution in both directions; 28 over the fit's
control, its two-maximum Top@1 against the sorted one ON A TIE, its LP's separability and its floor,
its stratified seeded folds, and its three tables.

**Shipped:** `scripts/terms-fit.py` (the ceiling, the fit, and the held-out report), the shared
`benchmarks/src/terms-dump.ts` writer now used by BOTH runners, `--terms-dump` on the RCAEval runner
and unconditionally on its workflow (it costs no second analysis there — `BenchmarkRunner` already
ranks over the whole node set — which is why the FSE'26 side stays opt-in).

**Acceptance test:** `Top@1 >= 1082` with no fault type down. **Still unmet**: the fitted vector
reaches 1204 in-sample but regresses `HTTPRequestAbort −2`, `HTTPRequestReplacePath −1` and
`HTTPResponsePatchBody −3`, and a default change additionally has to survive the RCAEval corpus
where `temporal` alone is documented at −40 pp. No end-of-programme signal.

**Readback of the instrument, and the two numbers it settled.** The FSE'26 dump (`43055506630`, 1422
cases, 69 688 candidate rows) reproduced its own run exactly — `1073/1227/1249` — so the screen's
arithmetic is the engine's, and the S1 unit hypothesis is **refuted at the shipped weights**
(`minmax` 1058, `rank` 833 against 1073). A per-case LP then answered the question the whole fortnight
of arms could not: **99.30 %** of cases admit a weight vector that ranks the answer first (100.00 %
with free signs), against **84.67 %** for the best single vector in-sample and **83.47 %** held-out.
The gap is heterogeneity, not capacity.

**And the admission rule holds the line.** Under "no fault type down" the best single vector is worth
**+1 case** (1074); the +131 is a trade — `ReplaceCode +62` and `ReplaceMethod +24` bought with
`PatchBody −3`, `Abort −2`, `Path −1`. A mixture over six label-free channel signatures reaches
**+112** held-out and lifts the corpus's worst regime (`-lat +failedEdge -log`, 159 cases, 34.6 %)
to 83.0 %, and still loses one case in three types, because the gate is applied per bucket while the
number that must clear is the mixture's. **Next: one joint coordinate ascent over all six vectors
with the corpus-level gate as the objective.**

**The cross-corpus gate, and it is decisive.** The RCAEval dump (`43120401664`, 735 cases = RE1 375 +
RE2 270 + RE3 90) reproduces its own cells exactly — RE1 `345/375` (92.00 %, the artifact's own printed
92.0 %), RE2 `248/270`, RE3 `71/90`, pooled **664/735 = 90.34 %**. Applying the FSE'26 vector of this
iteration WITHOUT refitting reads **604/735 = 82.18 %**: **−60 cases, −8.16 pp**, cell by cell −43/−8/−9.
So the coefficients are a property of the CORPUS and not of the mechanism, measured in the direction
that costs: a re-fit worth +8 pp on one benchmark is worth −8 pp on the other. Restoring one term at a
time does not recover it, and `prism` — which the fit switched ON — is worth **+75** there, so the
failure is not one bad term but a vector that belongs to another corpus. **No default changes.**

## Iteration 263 — the joint fit is the bucket fit, and the weight axis is closed

Iteration 262 named the next step as **one joint coordinate ascent over all six signature vectors
with the corpus-level gate as its objective**, and asserted it was "a different optimisation and not
a harder parameter search". It was implemented and it is **not different**: the joint climb returns
**1185/1422 held-out, the same total as the bucket-wise mixture, to the case**, and the gated variant
returns **1144, also identical**. The reason is structural and worth writing down, because it closes
the axis: a bucket's vector reaches only that bucket's rows, so a gain it makes is booked entirely
inside its own bucket, and an objective that sums over buckets has the same gradient as one that
scores the corpus. The joint form is 13× faster (14.8 s against 197 s per five folds, from a
row-restricted `scores_rows` and a cached control reading) and it states the objective correctly, and
that is all it does.

**The gate was the next hypothesis, and it fails in a way that generalises.** The gated joint fit
still loses three fault types, each by **exactly one case** (`NetworkLoss` 29→28, `PodFailure` 24→23,
`JVMCPUStress` 1→0) — but a _different_ three from the bucket-wise fit (`PodKill`, `NetworkDelay`).
The gate is not broken: it is evaluated on the training split and the report is on the held-out one,
and on a type with 24 cases one case is 4.2 pp with a standard deviation of about one case. **"No
fault type down on held-out" is not a property any training-time constraint can guarantee.** It is a
property of the corpus being large enough that the held-out count is stable, which 1 422 cases across
25 types is not.

**Shrinkage was the third attempt and it does not move them either.** Four strengths:

| shrink | ungated                 | gated              |
| ------ | ----------------------- | ------------------ |
| 1.00   | 1185 (+112), 3 down     | 1144 (+71), 3 down |
| 0.75   | **1187 (+114)**, 3 down | 1145 (+72), 3 down |
| 0.50   | 1175 (+102), 4 down     | 1135 (+62), 3 down |
| 0.25   | 1163 (+90), 2 down      | 1126 (+53), 3 down |

Shrinkage produced the programme's best held-out reading (**1187, +114**) and changed nothing about
the regressions, which is the definition of a bias that is not variance.

**And the mixture does not transfer, which closes the last route to a default.** The single vector of
262 transferred to RCAEval at −60 cases; the obvious reply was that the _signature_ is a label-free
routing key and would route better. It does not: **472/735 = 64.22 % against a 90.34 % control,
−192 cases (−26.12 pp)**, worse than the single vector. The bucket carrying 656 of RCAEval's 735
cases — the same `-lat -failedEdge -log` signature that carries 101 of FSE'26's — loses **191**. A
signature that identifies a bucket in both corpora and wants opposite coefficients in each is a
**corpus-internal routing key**, not a mechanism.

**Acceptance test:** `Top@1 >= 1082` with no fault type down. Read on the configuration that would
ship — one vector per signature, fitted on every case — the gated joint climb reaches
**1228/1422 = 86.36 % (+155)** with **zero fault types down among the gated population (≥ 4 cases)**;
the sole regression is `JVMCPUStress`, a one-case type that is 100 pp of noise and the reason
`--gate-types` exists as a separate floor. Two facts must be said in the same breath: that number is
**in-sample**, and the honest generalisation estimate is the **1144 (+71)** held-out reading, which
loses one case in each of two protected types. **No end-of-programme signal.**

**Therefore the next iteration is not a weight fit.** The per-case LP ceiling says 99.30 % of cases
are separable by _some_ non-negative vector; no single vector and no mixture over six channel
signatures exceeds 84.5 % held-out. The distance between those two numbers is not a function of the
slopes the engine already has — it is the distance between the information the engine measures and
the information the ranking needs. The next iteration is a **new measurable channel**, and
`docs/absent-census.md` names the population: the 159-case `-lat +failedEdge -log` bucket, worst
regime at 34.6 %, lifted to 83.0 % by its own vector and only to 61 % by a vector fitted elsewhere.

Full readings, the eight tables and the three refutations in derivation order: `architecture-audit-263.md`.

## Iteration 264 — the floor was a wall, and the wall was hiding thirty-six regressions

Iteration 263 concluded that no training-time constraint can keep a fault type whole on held-out data.
This iteration tested that as an **instrument** question and the answer is that the conclusion was true
and incomplete. `TypeGate` charges `n_cases + 1` per lost case — more than any total the corpus can
produce — so a coordinate ascent that starts inside the barrier never leaves it. The same rule with a
**finite per-type price, learnt by dual ascent**, and a **warm start** from the ungated optimum, reads
**1204 (+131)** where the barrier read **+1**. The admission test is unchanged; what changed is that the
search may walk through a violating state to reach an admissible one.

**The deficits are not where the rule looks.** The +131 vector's net table says three types down by
1–3 cases. The gross table says **36 cases lost and 167 gained**: `HTTPRequestAbort` loses five and
wins three (net −2), `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` gains sixty-six and loses four (net +62, four regressions
unreported). A rule over counts is therefore **too strict** — it refused +131 over two net cases — and
**too lax** — a level net would have admitted all thirty-six.

**So the strict form was built and measured: `CaseFloor`, no case the control answers may be lost.**
Over ten configurations (hard and soft, cold and warm, prices to 10⁹) the best reading that preserves
every control-won case is **1074 (+1)**, and every serious gain hands back 17 to 36. **No monotone vector
exists in the neighbourhood**: the shipped default is on the Pareto frontier of `(Top@1, cases
preserved)`, and the frontier is steep — 113 cases cost 17 regressions.

**Why, measured rather than argued.** The 36 lost cases are the thin wins, and none of them is a tie
(0 of 1073 control-won cases is won by less than 10⁻⁹). Median won margin **0.947**, median lost margin
**0.260**, thinnest **0.0063**, 16 of 36 inside the bottom decile. The term that flips each one is
`prism` (13), `failedEdge` (10), `temporal` (7), `lat` (3) — the same twelve coordinates the gains are
made of. The score is linear in the weights, the no-loss region is the intersection of 1 073 half-spaces,
and the shipped point lies six thousandths from its nearest boundary.

**The margin surrogate confirms the diagnosis from a third direction.** `Top@1` is only the sign of the
margin, so `Σ tanh(margin/τ)` was fitted instead: best reading of the programme (**1212, +139**, τ = 0.1)
and not one deficit repaired.

**Acceptance test: not met.** No vector is shipped; the reading is unchanged at 1073. The next iteration
is not a weight fit and not a new rule — it is a **coordinate that is zero on the cases the ranking wins
thinly**, so its contribution can rise where it must without moving the marginal ones. That is the
fault-free baseline frequency channel of Lee et al. (2026, arXiv 2611.02416).

Full readings, the eight tables and the four refutations in derivation order: `architecture-audit-264.md`.

## Iteration 265 — the coordinate that is not in the case

Iteration 264 closed with a shape rather than a gain: _a coordinate that is zero on the cases the ranking wins
thinly_. This iteration built it — the **fault-free frequency** prior of Lee et al. (arXiv 2611.02416, §4.1.1), the
fraction of fault-free windows in which a channel's own anomaly leaves a three-σ band — and reports **no shipped
change**.

**The departure the corpus forces, and it is the one that makes the measurement possible.** The paper profiles 18 to
211 hours of fault-free operation; a datapack here is one recording with one injection time. But the same
`(service, channel)` pair re-appears in every case that touches that service, and each case's pre-segment is
fault-free by construction. **A case is one window**, the rate is counted over the cases that carried the channel,
and a corpus of `n` cases gives an `n`-window rate. Weaker than the paper's 10-minute windowing in one direction —
a channel that swings within a case but holds its level across cases reads as clean — stronger in another: no
boundary choice can bias a window that is a whole pre-segment.

**The mechanism exists, and it was measured before it was wired.** On the 131 RCAEval datapacks whose raw metrics
are local: 138 channels published, `r` spanning the whole range (quantiles 0 / 0.077 / **0.332** / 0.686 / 1), 31
channels that never fired and 22 that fired in every fault-free window they were ever observed in. The two ends are
the two populations the term exists to separate: `frontend_mem` and three `*_latency` at `r = 0` against
`front-end_cpu`, `orders-db_cpu`, `rabbitmq_cpu` and `catalogue_workload` at `r = 1`.

**It is not a ranker, and the paper's own baseline says so.** Ordering by `r` alone reads 12.3 % Top@1 against ~7 %
uniform; the paper's "Statistical EOB" baseline reads 7.1 % Exact on Bank and its headline belongs to a model
reading the profile as context. **The term therefore enters as one slope in the fusion, not as a re-ranker.**

**As an added coordinate, on the 130 cases that are local: one case.** Shipped score + `w · (1 − r_e)` reads
90.8 % → **91.5 %** at `w ∈ [0.1, 0.3]`, and degrades past 0.5 (89.2 / 86.9 / 78.5 / 60.8 at 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.2 / 2.0).
A one-case move at n = 130 is 0.77 pp and spans zero — and the population is the wrong one: RE1:OnlineBoutique, where
the engine already reads 90.8 %, while the 349 cases this term was built for live in RE3:TrainTicket and the FSE'26
archive.

**Acceptance test: not met**, and nothing ships. `DEFAULT_FAULT_FREE_WEIGHT = 0`; the ranking is bit-identical to
the engine that had no such term (asserted, not argued — the same corpus with a profile at 0 and with no profile
produces the same order). The standing anchor's digest moved only because the reported line gained the two fields
that name the term at their defaults; the nine cells are predicted unmoved in `docs/sota-comparison.md` §0p-v.

**The next iteration is the two-arm dispatch**, and it is cheap because the profile is an artifact: build it once per
corpus, run the control and one arm on the same file with `--terms-dump`, and read the **held-out** number from
`scripts/terms-fit.py --only repair`. The prediction to be wrong about is stated: on the FSE'26 archive the prior
moves the **absent** bucket (173 cases) far more than the top-1 bucket.

**Two defects the guards found, and neither was the one being looked for.** The projections build the profile key
CONDITIONALLY because `forwarded ∪ nonEngine = parsed` is asserted over key SETS and the profile is a second
argument rather than a parsed option — assigning it unconditionally broke six guards in three packages, which is how
that was learned rather than argued. And the profile builder's argument chain ended at its last `else if`, so a
mistyped `--min-sample 8` left the sample floor at its default and published a band fitted at a threshold nobody
typed; it now refuses an unknown token by name. Both were found by coverage — an uncovered arm and an uncovered
`else` — which is the second iteration running in which the coverage gate located a real bug rather than a metric.

Full readings, the two measurement tables and the design notes: `architecture-audit-265.md`.

## Iteration 266 — the axis this register closed, reopened in the one shape it left room for

**The entry at line 145 ends with a sentence that is also an instruction: a reopening needs the presentation to
change, not the weight.** Two iterations then spent their whole budget on `faultFreeWeight` — a weight. The axis was
not reopened; it was walked past. This iteration builds the reopening.

**Three things differ from `0d6ae609`, and each is why the earlier verdict cannot be transferred.**

| dimension    | what `0d6ae609` measured                                       | what this layer will measure                                                                                    |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| population   | RE3:TrainTicket's three error-value families, ~30 cases        | **RCABench, all 1 422**, plus the nine RCAEval cells                                                            |
| shape        | a ReAct loop walking an evidence dump with a retrieval toolkit | a **typed elimination claim** the engine verifies, or `abstain`                                                 |
| presentation | unchanged                                                      | a **fingerprint**: ≤5 candidates × ≤8 channels × 5 numbers, ~1 600 tokens against the retired layer's 1 500 000 |

**The 90.0 % that motivated the question decomposes, and the decomposition is why this is not a copy.** `arXiv:
2608.21310` Table 2 reads 42.6 % → 90.0 % across ten configurations, and its own sections price the gap four ways:
the population is a **500-case random sample**, not the 1 422; the top-band frameworks span **2.0 pp** (79.2 / 79.6
/ 77.6) while swapping Sonnet for Qwen moves **10.8 pp**, i.e. the backbone is five times the design; the paper's
own reconstruction ceiling is **√Edge F1 ≤ 0.67** even on correct localisations; and its defence prototype reads
**43.5 % → 52.5 %** in an independent setting. Our second-path reading on this corpus is **42.69 %**, level with the
worst name in that table — and the table contains **no non-LLM method at all**, so "4th in the agentic panel" was
never the right sentence about where this engine stands.

**Two roles, because the axis that separates them has no control in any published table.** `eliminator` anchors on
the engine's top-K and may only remove or promote a candidate with a claim that re-derives from the fingerprint;
`investigator` decides what to look at and when to stop. The trajectory study's Finding 1 is that no top agent was
built for RCA and every purpose-built one trails — which is a claim about the eliminator's ceiling, and it is only
falsifiable here because the eliminator sits on a ranker that is not an LLM.

**The cost is a structural claim, not a discount.** Fingerprint instead of dump (166×), three rounds instead of
45–54 (15×), a deterministic skip rule over cases the engine already leads clearly (~2×), and a model chosen for a
numeric comparison rather than for judgement (~10×). Worked at list prices the eliminator is **$5.3 for all 1 422
cases** against the published $284, and after the first run the cache makes every ablation **$0**. None of those
terms removes a case from the scope: the 500-case arm is **stratified** on fault family × engine correctness ×
causal-chain depth, so it is the same benchmark at a smaller n, and the published 90.0 % rests on a random 500.

**Four flags, and the default is off.** `--agentic-mode` (`off` | `eliminator` | `investigator`),
`--agentic-weight`, `--agentic-budget` (rounds, tokens, µ$), `--agentic-model`. `weight = 0` means the layer does
not run — not that it runs and is ignored — and an integration test asserts the ranking is bit-identical to the
engine that has no agentic code.

**What is built this iteration, and what is not.** Built and measured: the bounded hypothesis space and its claim
verifier (`packages/ai/src/agent/hypothesis-space.ts`, 28 tests), the three-gate budget ledger
(`budget.ts`, 24 tests), and the stratified sampler (`benchmarks/src/agentic-sampling.ts`, 26 tests) — all at
100 % on all four coverage dimensions. Not built: the runner wiring, the cache, and the dispatch. **No score moved
this iteration**, so there is nothing here to enrol.

**Two defects the coverage gate found in this iteration's own code, both real.** The floor can overspend — a
stratum smaller than the floor takes only what it holds while its neighbours still take the full floor — so an arm
announced as 500 cases could have run 502; the clawback now takes the excess from the strata ABOVE their floor,
because taking it from the smallest would have cut a two-case family to one to pay for a two-hundred-case family,
which is the vanishing the plan exists to prevent. And the sampler accepted a corpus holding the same case twice,
which would have weighted one case double in the arm's accuracy and shown nowhere in the coverage table.

Full design, cost model and acceptance criteria: `docs/agentic-layer-plan.md`.

## Iteration 267 — the ceiling is real, the deterministic arms are not, and the axis closes in one of them

**Three arms ran, they cost nothing, and they disagree.** On 711 converted RCABench cases (the `waveB2` half; the
other half is not converted in this environment) the shipped engine reads **68.07 %** Top@1 and **84.81 %** Top@5.
A perfect eliminator that may only remove a candidate by a **verifiable** claim — channel outside its band on the
removed candidate, present on both — reaches **84.70 %**. That is **+16.63 pp**, with zero refused claims, over 118
cases, and 3 rounds suffice for 95 % of them.

**So the layer is not chasing a rounding error, and the ceiling is not a matter of opinion.** It is also **bounded
by the posterior's recall**: the ceiling equals Top@5 to within one case, because an eliminator can only reorder
inside the five candidates it is given. 108 cases (15.2 %) are unreachable for a reason no layer can fix — the truth
never entered the posterior — and those belong to the ranking, not to this axis.

**The expected-outlier rate, stated as an elimination RULE rather than as a weight, is refused.** The rule demotes a
leader whose least ordinary channel leaves its fault-free band in most clean windows, in favour of a rival whose
evidence is rarer. Swept over six floors and three margins on a hash split: the most permissive setting reads
**46.3 %** (−21.8 pp, 310 moves); the best held-out setting reads **68.2 %** against the engine's **68.75 %** there,
i.e. four moves and −0.6 pp. That is the third presentation of one quantity to fail — additive term (iteration 265,
+1 case, CI crosses zero), elimination rule (here), and the column that survives because its job is to make a claim
_checkable_ rather than to decide it. **The decider is closed.** The mechanical reason is in the census: mean
channel rate 0.749, median 0.796, and only **0.8 %** of channels clean — on this corpus "left its band" is not a
rare event, so a rate that counts it does not order two candidates by how surprising their evidence is.

**The skip rule is refused too, and it was the cost model's 2× term.** `top1_margin > 5 % ∨ out-of-band channels ≥ 3`
skips **710 of 711** cases — and with them **117 of the 118** a perfect eliminator could fix. Relaxing it does not
help: the most selective gate in the grid (margin 1.0, 8 channels) still discards 85 fixable cases, **72 % of the
headroom**, to save 138 calls. A fixable case is mechanically a case where a _symptom_ outranks the source
confidently, so a wide margin is evidence **for** consultation. The honest spend is the full corpus at **$5.3**; the
54× gap to the published $284 stands, the extra 2× does not, and the plan is amended rather than left carrying a
saving a measurement refused.

**What ships, and what it is worth.** The fingerprint builder, its dump and the offline analyzer — 100 % on all four
coverage dimensions, 96 new assertions across four modules — plus two refusals that stop the next iteration from
spending money on either. No score moved on a published configuration this iteration; what moved is the size of the
prize, from "unknown" to **+16.63 pp measured with a stated ceiling and a stated round budget**.

**Design corrections recorded rather than papered over.** The builder lives in `benchmarks`, not in `tree` as
`agentic-layer-plan.md` §7 said: it joins the case's metrics, the engine's posterior and the corpus profile, and its
output type belongs to `packages/ai`, so `tree` would have had to import `ai` or duplicate the type — the diagram's
own forbidden edge. And two guards the fingerprint module carried could not fire (a non-finite departure, and the
`NaN` arm of the sort comparator): every sample is checked finite before a median is taken, so the guards were dead
branches of the kind this repository deletes rather than documents.

Full readings, the census, the gate grid and the reproduction commands: `docs/agentic-headroom.md`.

## Iteration 270 — the ceiling was the width of the window, and the bucket named "absent" was not

The elimination layer was priced against `Top@5` and the price was written down as `+12.19 pp` over 1 422 cases.
That is a true statement about a five-wide presentation and a false one about the ranking. `--depth-out` dumps
where the corpus's answer sits in the order the engine actually sorted, and a stratified 106-case reading of it
finds the answer **somewhere in the order in 1 422 of 1 422 cases** — median miss depth 4, maximum 44, **zero
absent** (`docs/agentic-headroom.md` §10). Over a twenty-wide window the reachable ceiling is **92.12 %**, i.e.
**+16.66 pp** against the control rather than +12.19 pp. (A 106-case pilot put that window at 97.2 %; it drew 3 of
the 112 cases past twenty and is recorded as the pilot's error rather than as the ceiling.)

**Closed: the fingerprint COLUMNS as a tie-break decider.** Over the 176 cases a perfect eliminator can fix, none of
the five columns separates the source from the wrong leader: the source's onset is earlier in 87/176 (49.4 %, exact
binomial p = 0.94), its largest deviation is larger in 102/176 (58.0 %, p = 0.042 before the correction for four
columns), its minimum fault-free rate is lower in 85/176 (48.3 %, p = 0.71), and its outside-band channel count is
_equal_ in 111/176 (63.1 %). Each column used as the PRIMARY signal scores 26–34 % against the engine's 75.9 %, and
the best gated top-1/top-2 tie-break over four keys and seven margins moves **+0.14 pp held out — one case in 709**,
while every wider gate loses. That does not close a model that reasons across the columns jointly; it closes the
claim that the columns carry the split, which is what the presentation change was supposed to deliver.

**Reinterpreted, not reopened: the `absent` bucket.** `docs/absent-census.md`'s 173 cases are absent from the
reported FIVE, and the document's opening paragraph read that as absent from the candidate SET ("no coefficient of a
term it never entered can reach it"). The depth reading refutes the second reading and leaves the first intact: those
cases are _deep_, their owner is ordering — the same owner the `top5` bucket has — and the document's own §4
diagnostic had already said so ("the service is **not invisible** … it loses because every competitor carries
more"). The bucket keeps its count and loses its inference.

**Opened, with a kill criterion written before the data:** `docs/depth-reranking-preregistration.md`. If no term in
the engine's own sum favours the truth in ≥ 65 % of a family's deep cases (n ≥ 20, Bonferroni over 18 terms), the
term axis closes and the depth headroom belongs to a model arm over a twenty-wide presentation.

## Iteration 271 — the term axis, measured against a bar written before the data; and the denominator was short by one

`docs/depth-reranking-preregistration.md` was executed as one dispatch (`43334354978`, `--terms-dump` over all
1 422 cases, the report printed in the same job). The measurement found **two defects in the instrument and none in
the engine**, and both were the kind that produce a plausible table rather than an error.

**Defect 1 — the formula has nineteen terms and the pre-registration counted eighteen.** The report's own fence
refused the first dispatch by name: `the dump carries terms the pre-registration does not count: victim`. `victim`
is PRISM's symmetry mask — subtracted, not added, and written across four lines of `buildTerm(`, so the single-line
scan that produced `DECLARED_TERMS` could not see it, and the guard test asserted the list against _the same scan_,
which is a fence that agrees with its object. The correction is applied in the stricter direction: `α = 0.05/19 =
0.002632`, because a denominator that grew while `α` stood still only makes every cell harder to clear, and
re-basing `α` to keep an eighteen-term reading alive would be the post-hoc adjustment the document forbids.

**Defect 2 — the population boundary was off by one.** `depth ≤ 20` admitted the twenty-first candidate while
`recall@20` counts `depth < 20`; the first reading therefore reported **241** misses against a ladder whose `@20`
rung implies **237**. Corrected, the population reconciles exactly: `1 073` correct at one, `237` re-rankable
misses, `112` past the window, `1 422` cases. The instrument that caught the first defect could not catch this one
— it was caught by comparing the report against a table published before it — which is why the population
statement is printed above the tables rather than inferred from them.

**What the population is, once both are fixed.** 237 misses at depth 1–20 of 1 422 cases, and **all 237 reconstruct
their `finalScore` from their terms exactly** (worst residual `0.0`), so the dump is lossless and no share below is a
description of a truncated sum. The depth derived from the term dump of _this_ run agrees with the depth artifact of
the _agentic_ run (`43276123043`) on **1 422 of 1 422 cases, zero disagreements** — two dispatches, one order.

**The §2 statistic, pooled over the 237 (this is the fraction of misses on which the term pays the truth more):**

| term               | measurable | favours truth |      share | exact two-sided p | in-half | out-half |
| ------------------ | ---------: | ------------: | ---------: | ----------------: | ------: | -------: |
| `stability`        |        216 |           147 | **68.1 %** |          `< 1e-4` |  75.0 % |   61.1 % |
| `lat`              |        104 |            72 | **69.2 %** |          `0.0001` |  61.2 % |   76.4 % |
| `selfAnomalyLog1p` |        235 |            60 |     25.5 % |          `< 1e-4` |  21.1 % |   29.8 % |
| `log`              |        133 |            14 |     10.5 % |          `< 1e-4` |  13.6 % |    8.1 % |
| `dualFamily`       |         73 |            23 |     31.5 % |          `0.0021` |  22.6 % |   38.1 % |
| `pool`             |         18 |             6 |     33.3 % |          `0.2379` |  50.0 % |   12.5 % |
| `failedEdge`       |          8 |             4 |     50.0 % |          `1.0000` |  33.3 % |   60.0 % |

**Twelve of the nineteen terms are not live on this population at all** — `source`, `temporal`, `collision`,
`topo`, `rise`, `trace`, `prism`, `faultFree`, `selfTime`, `emission`, `victim` and `podState` were measurable on
zero misses — which is itself a reading: the ranking that loses these 237 cases is decided by **seven terms**, and
by **four** of them on more than sixty cases each.

The structure is not a fishing expedition: five readings clear `α = 0.002632` on a population of 237, they point in
two opposite directions (_the two tuned priors favour the truth; the base term, the log term and the dual-family
indicator favour the symptom_), and every one of them replicates in both halves of the pre-registered split.

**The §3 action bar — the pre-registered unit — names exactly one cell, and it does not survive the grid.**
`stability @ HTTPResponseReplaceCode` clears in-sample (13/14 = 92.9 %, p = 0.0018) and keeps its sign held out
(5/7 = 71.4 %). But the table scans **114 cells** (six families at n ≥ 20 × nineteen terms), and `0.05/114 =
4.4e-4`; at that level the cell fails, and the expected number of false positives over the grid at the
pre-registered per-family `α` is `114 × 0.002632 ≈ 0.30`. So the honest statement is that **one cell cleared a bar
that did not account for how many cells were scanned**, and the document's own kill criterion does not reach it.

**Closed: the per-family term correction.** The pre-registration's partial-result clause licenses "a per-family
term correction … measured as one". It is refused here, on its own terms, because the cell that would license it
does not clear the correction over the number of cells the measurement actually scanned. A correction fitted to
one family of 23 cases at `p = 0.0018` in a 114-cell grid is the fitted artifact the document's §5.3 exists to
prevent.

**NOT closed: the term axis itself, and the reason is the pooled table.** H1 said the lead a symptom holds is
concentrated in a small set of terms with a stable sign. On the pre-registered _family_ unit that is not
established. On the pre-registered _statistic_ (§2, pooled) it is: two tuned priors favour the truth in ~68–69 %
of misses while the base term favours the winner in 74.5 %, and the log term favours the winner in 89.5 %. The
mechanism this describes is not "a term is mispaid on one family" but "the base term decides, and the priors that
are right are priced too low to matter" — which is a **global** question, and one the repository already has
machinery for (`latent-term-census.ts` computes the weight at which each term wins a case back, and
`docs/base-term-price.md` holds the base term's sweep).

**Priced the same day, and CLOSED: the global weight axis.** The counterfactual is arithmetic over the same dump —
`score′(v) = score(v) + Σ Δw·slope(v)` — so the landscape costs no dispatch. It reproduces the published
**1 073 / 1 422 = 75.46 %** exactly at `Δw = 0`, which is what entitles it to be read at all, and then it returns an
**empty admissible set**: every point in a 30-point grid that gains a case takes one from a family with n ≥ 20, and
the shipped `stability = 0.007352`, `lat = 0.561495`, `log = 1.0` is the only measured point that loses nothing.
`stability → 0.2` is `+4` with three families down; `lat → 0.4` is `−6`; `log → 0.8` is `−29`.

> **Corrected at iteration 272, on the screen's own output.** The set is empty only among points that **gain**;
> `stability → 0` and `stability → 0.02` also lose nothing, because they change nothing (0 gained, 0 lost), and a
> gate written as "`Top@1` must not fall" always admits the identity. The per-family counts above were also
> incomplete: `stability → 0.2` costs **six** families (not three) and `lat → 0.4` costs **five** (not four).
> `docs/term-weight-landscape.md` §3.1 and §3.3.

**And it falsifies the reading above, in the direction that matters.** `log` pays the _symptom_ more on 89.5 % of
the misses where it is measurable — `p < 1e-4`, the largest weight in the sum leaning that way — and cutting its
weight is still the most destructive move on the board (`−225` at 0.3). A term can be wrong about the cases one is
looking at and worth its weight on the cases one is not; the decomposition describes the 237, it is not a gradient.
Recorded, not shipped, and **not** a proposal: `stability 0.3 + log 1.2` is worth **+13 cases (76.37 %)** and fails
the gate by three cases across two families.

> **Corrected at iteration 272: eight families above the floor and 12 cases — 14 lost in total, the other two in
> families below the floor — against `+27` gained.** Three cases against two families reads as a near miss worth
> arguing about; fourteen against eight is a point that moves eight of the corpus's fault families the wrong way.
> `docs/term-weight-landscape.md` §3.3.

**What that leaves.** The admissible set is empty because the same 237 misses want opposite things — raising
`stability` recovers `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` and `NetworkBandwidth` while costing `HTTPRequestDelay` and
`NetworkPartition`. No single weight vector can have both, and the only conditional rules this register admits are
ones with a mechanism rather than a fitted per-family constant. So the remaining headroom is **not reachable by
re-weighting the terms the formula already has**; what is left is a term that does not exist yet, or a reader that
sees more than a weighted sum of the live ones — which is the model arm, and why the depth window matters.
Full landscape, grid and reproduction: `docs/term-weight-landscape.md`.

**Also read this iteration, and it moves the standings page rather than this register:** `docs/rcatlas-crosswalk.md`
— the field's first unified 90-case benchmark (`arXiv:2610.35767`) read down to its per-source cell, including the
27-case RCAEval column this engine can already be placed in.

## Iteration 272 — the landscape promoted from a script to a module, and the three things that changed when it could be run

`docs/term-weight-landscape.md` published the weight landscape at 271 from a 60-line script that lived outside the
tree, and its own §4 said the next iteration would promote it. That is what happened:
`benchmarks/src/term-weight-screen.ts` (module: `prepareCases` / `evaluatePrepared` / `screenPrepared` / `screenGrid`
/ `formatScreenReport` / `parseGridFile` / `parseScreenArgs`), `benchmarks/src/run-term-weight-screen.ts` (console),
and 47 tests. The screen reads the same 40 MB dump of run `43334354978` and reproduces **1 073 / 1 422 = 75.46 %**
at `Δw = 0` with **0 of 1 422 cases refused** — the reconstruction identity `Σ (w × slope) = finalScore` holds on
every candidate of every case, worst residual `0.0`.

**What the promotion bought is not the code, it is three corrections the script could not make.** They are the
reason a screen belongs in the tree: a script that aggregates into a printed string can only print what it was
written to collect, and nothing about the printed string says what it left out.

**Correction 1 — the admissible set was not empty.** `stability → 0` and `stability → 0.02` lose nothing because
they change nothing: 0 gained, 0 lost, the same 1 073 cases in the same order. "`Top@1` must not fall" is satisfied
by the identity, so the set of points that pass it always contains the identity's neighbourhood, and "the admissible
set is empty" was true only among points that gain. The module therefore reports ADMISSIBLE and **NO-OP**
separately and names the no-ops under the verdict, because "worth 0 cases" and "worth 13" are not two answers to
one question. The third zero-net row is the reason the no-op test is the gross counts and not the net:
`log → 1.2` is 6 gained against 6 lost — a wash that still takes four cases from `HTTPRequestDelay`.

**Correction 2 — the published "families that lose" column understated every refusal.** `stability 0.3 + log 1.2`
was published as failing in two families by three cases; the screen says **eight families above the floor and 12
cases**, 14 lost in total (`HTTPRequestDelay −2`, `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod −1`, `HTTPRequestReplacePath −2`,
`HTTPResponseDelay −3`, `HTTPResponseReplaceCode −1`, `JVMException −1`, `JVMReturn −1`, `NetworkPartition −1`, and
`+2` in families below the floor). `stability → 0.2` was three families and is six; `stability → 0.4` was "five
families, −8 in total" and is eleven families and 26 (28 lost in total); `lat → 0.4` was four and is five. The
formatter cannot print a family it was not given, so the column cannot understate a row without the row being wrong
— and the losses it does not list are now printed as a `(+N below the floor)` remainder, so every row's arithmetic
adds up on its face.

**New, and it is the strongest form of the negative result this register has.** The `gained/lost` column makes the
shape of the landscape quantitative: **13 of the 28 grid points gain at least one case, and every one of the 13 loses
at least one.** There is no strict improvement anywhere on the grid — not one case gained for free. The best net,
`+13`, is 27 gained against 14 lost: **41 cases change hands to move the total by 13**. Across the 13 gaining
points the ratio of gross exchange to net gain runs from **3.0** to **57**, with a median of exactly **6.0**. So the
population does not contain a direction of improvement with a slope; it contains a near-cancellation, which is why
searching the weights harder cannot find one — every step trades cases at roughly 4–6 to 1.

**Closed, and closed more firmly than at 271: the global weight axis.** No point on the 28-point grid gains a case
without losing one, and the points that lose nothing are the points that do nothing. Under the pre-registered gate
(`Top@1` must not fall; no family with `n ≥ 20` may lose a case the shipped run answered) the admitted set is
**empty**. The three live weights are confirmed as the measured zero-regression point for the second time, now from
the repository's own code rather than from a script beside it.

**Also settled here, and it is a fact about the formula rather than about the landscape:** twelve of the nineteen
terms carry weight 0 in the shipped configuration — seven recorded as `0` (`collision`, `failedEdge`, `prism`,
`rise`, `source`, `temporal`, `topo`) and five absent from the dump entirely (`trace`, `faultFree`, `selfTime`,
`emission`, `victim`). The shipped ranking is a sum of **seven** weighted terms, and the grid moves three of them.

> **Corrected at iteration 277.** `failedEdge` is not a zero. It ships at **3** and records `0` on the 1 114 cases
> its gate refused, so the shipped ranking is a sum of seven weighted terms on those cases and of **eight** on the
> 108 the gate admitted — and the two arms it implies are worth 1 031 and 1 096 against a run that scores 1 073.
> `recorded-configuration.md` §2 gives the theorem (`w = max S`) and §4 the per-family ablation. The paragraph's
> count of zero-weight terms is therefore fourteen minus one, not fourteen.

**What that leaves, unchanged in direction and now measured in size.** The remaining 237 misses are not reachable by
re-weighting the terms the formula already has: what is left is a term that does not exist yet (a new observable) or
a reader that sees more than a weighted sum of the seven — which is the model arm, and why the depth window matters.
Full grid, all 28 points with gross counts: `docs/term-weight-landscape.md` §2–§3.

## Iteration 273 — the decay law falsified by reading it, and the direction picked instead of the one proposed

The 271 and 272 reflections both named the same next axis: replace the fitted `decayAlpha`/`decayBeta` with Deng Yu's
graph-expansion suppression `α = ε^k`. It was approved, and the first thing this iteration did was look at where the
parameters are read. **Both are out of the ranking**, and `docs/loop-decay-falsified.md` records the three routes and
closes each: the score sum (`childContrib` is excluded from the ranking deliberately — `pruner.ts:3108`), the cycle
contribution (a second α the caller cannot set, and no term carries it), and pruning (`pruneCycles` reads
`propagationWeight`, not contribution).

**The measurement is one probe and eight lines:** at `α = 0.2` and `α = 0.95` on a graph with exactly one
three-cycle, the ranking, the scores and every term are **bit-identical** (`1.162317861, 0.702659439, 0.382419815,
0.142307949`), and the only fields that move are `propagationErrorBound = 1 − α^depth` and the `confidence` derived
from it. α moves the uncertainty the engine states, not what it states.

**Closed: the decay law as a ranking lever.** A parameter no score reads cannot be improved by a theorem, and the
271 reflection's error was inferring a lever from a parameter's NAME and docstring without checking the data path. It
is worth naming the error precisely, because it is the same error the register's preamble describes from the other
side: a claim was taken from a name (`decayAlpha`, "1-hop decay factor"; the docstring even says "mean free path
attenuation") rather than from the arithmetic.

**What survives, and it is the sharper question.** The theorem becomes measurable the moment a cycle contribution is
a **term in the sum** — with a weight and a slope — because then `α` versus `ε^k` is a difference in the term's
shape. But that reopens the **directional-source row** first: a cycle is a direction-of-explanation quantity, and the
sign of those inverts between populations (`re3-fault-ceiling.md` measured RE3 SockShop 9/10 reversed against
TrainTicket's mirror). So the honest framing is not "a decay law" but "a term that would need both populations
measured before it has a law".

**The fence is the deliverable.** `packages/tree/__tests__/unit/decay-parameter-jurisdiction.test.ts` (8 tests) pins
the asymmetry rather than the absence: the answer is bit-identical at the two extremes, the stated uncertainty is
not, the bound is exactly `1 − α^depth`, the cycle contribution is `∏ p × 0.9³` for a three-cycle in a four-node
graph, the cycle α ignores the option, and no term is named after a cycle. Each of the three reopen conditions above
turns one assertion red, so the axis reopens deliberately or not at all.

**Cost.** Ten minutes of reading and a probe, against a 55-minute dispatch and a pre-registration that would have
been written first. This is the first axis in the project stopped by the register's own discipline _before_ it reached
a table.

## Iteration 274 — the resolution floor: the first measured improvement this register refuses to take

Iteration 272 closed the global weight axis on a 28-point grid whose smallest non-zero weight was `0.02`. That is a
statement about an interval, not about weights, and the gap is not academic: the twelve terms with weight 0 are
revived at exactly the magnitudes the grid never visited. So this iteration measured the weight at which a term
_begins_ to be able to change anything — `δ = gap / Δslope` minimised over the corpus, from the dump in one pass — and
then swept below the old floor with it.

**`benchmarks/src/weight-resolution.ts`** (`resolutionOf` / `resolutionPrepared` / `resolutionTable` / `termsOf` /
`formatResolutionReport` / `parseResolutionArgs`), `run-weight-resolution.ts`, 44 tests, **100 % of statements,
branches, functions and lines**. Three decisions make the number exact and each is a test: a hit is skipped; a case
where the term pays the leader at least as much is skipped; the comparison is **strict**, because at exactly
`gap / Δslope` the candidates are level and the engine's stable sort keeps the leader first.

**What it found first is a correction to itself.** The draft said "below the floor the term is a no-op". The RE1
reading falsified it: `prism` at `0.01` recovers nothing there — its floor is `7.2e-2` — and **costs two cases**. A
floor bounds what a term can **pay**, never what it can **cost**. The asymmetry is now a docstring, a line on every
report, and a test (`is gain-free, not event-free`).

**Four readings that were not available before:**

- **`podState` cannot recover a single one of the 420 misses across the four populations, at any weight**, and it
  carries weight `8` — more than the other six live terms combined. The heaviest term in the formula has no headroom
  on any miss.
- **`stability`'s floor moves by a factor of 30** across the four populations (`9.95e-3` RE3 → `3.03e-1` RE1).
- **`lat` and `pool` have no headroom on any RCAEval suite** (33 and 14 cases of it on RCABench): the latency term is
  not a recovery lever on the battery the project is ranked on.
- **`temporal`'s floor is `0.905` on RE3 and `1.69e-3` on RE1** — the same weight is a no-op on TrainTicket and
  decisive on OnlineBoutique.

**The sweep, at full resolution: 84 points × 4 populations = 336 readings.** The four gainful sets are **disjoint**.
Four points are admissible everywhere, and each is worth **one case on one population** — `temporal 0.003` on RE1,
`prism 0.005` on FSE'26, `collision 0.02`/`0.03` on RE2 — jointly **+3 over 2 157 with no loss anywhere**, each
holding over a window of two to six times its own magnitude. **This iteration does not take it**, and the reason is a
measurement rather than a preference: the near-tie census shows only **4 / 4 / 3 / 1** misses per population at a gap
≤ `1e-2`, so the whole population a revival at that scale can reach is **12 cases**, and three unrelated terms each
recovering one of them on a different population is what sampling twelve near-ties four times over produces. A
mechanism would concentrate on one term and one family and scale with the weight; these do neither. Three constants
of `0.003`, `0.006` and `0.02` each buying one case off a near-tie is the defect class
`ranking-default-owners.md` records.

The two candidates that looked like mechanism, and what each died of. **`prism 0.02`**: +3 on FSE'26 and on both
held-out halves (`+2` in, `+1` out), then **−4 on RCAEval RE1** (`delay −1`, `loss −3`), +2 on RE2 with a loss, +1 on
RE3 → **−1 over the 735**. The closure in `prism-pooling-frontier.md` survives being asked **two orders of magnitude
below the weights it was taken at**. **`temporal 0.04`**: **+5 on the `in` half and −1 on the `out` half** — a term
whose sign flips between two random halves of one corpus is not a term.

**Also closed here, and it was free — the pod/node observable as a source of information on this corpus.**
`injection.json` carries `ground_truth.pod` and `.container` in **1 422 of 1 422 packs** and
`scripts/convert-rcabench-to-rcaeval.py` keeps only `.service`, so a pod-level answer exists and is discarded. But the
deployment is **single-replica**: 48 pods to 48 workloads with 0 surplus, and of the 123 pod-identity faults
(`container-kill` 89, `pod-failure` 24, `pod-kill` 10) not one has a service with two pods. Pod identity is a
bijection with service identity here, so a per-pod signal separates nothing a per-service signal does not.
**RCAtlas's 31 pod/node-annotated cases still need RCAtlas's data**, and what would make them scoreable is an
answer-format mapping — a capability, recorded, not this iteration's subject.

**What the four screens now say together.** Weight: any point that gains a case loses one, 3–57× gross against net.
Landscape: no direction of improvement with a slope. Revival: the gainful sets are disjoint and worth 0.14 pp in
total. Resolution: the whole reachable population at revival scale is 12 cases in 2 157, and the rest of the misses
sit at gaps of `0.1` to `1`. The remaining misses are not reachable by re-weighting, reviving or re-shaping the
nineteen terms the formula has — only by a term with a different **shape**, and the pod census says this corpus cannot
supply one.

## Iteration 275 — the weight axis REOPENS: 274's closing sentence was a statement about axes, not about the dimension

> **Corrected at iteration 275.** The paragraph above ends _"the remaining misses are not reachable by re-weighting,
> reviving or re-shaping the nineteen terms the formula has — only by a term with a different shape"_. The first half of
> that sentence is **false**. Every screen behind it — 28 single-term points, 84 revival points, the resolution floor —
> moves ONE term, or a handful, and reads the corpus. Those are points on the axes of a 14-dimensional space. A
> direction that moves every term at once was never tested, and the test is not a sweep: it is a convex-hull question
> with an exact answer per case.

### The theorem, and the certificate on each side of it

`score(v) = Σᵢ wᵢ·vᵢ` is linear in `v`, so if the accepted candidate's vector `a` is a convex combination of the
competitors' — `a = Σ λᵢ vᵢ`, `λ` on the simplex — then for every `w`, `w·a ≤ maxᵢ w·vᵢ`, and `a` can only be first on a
**tie**, which the engine's stable sort resolves against it. If `a` is outside the hull, the separating hyperplane
theorem hands a witness. Reachability is therefore decided per case, not sampled, and `benchmarks/src/
weight-reachability.ts` decides it by maximising the margin over `(vᵢ − a)·w + t ≤ 0`, `|w| ≤ 1` — reading the
separator off the primal at `t > 0` and the hull combination off the **duals** at `t = 0`. Both come from one tableau.

Every verdict is then checked by substitution, which is what makes the numbers below claims rather than solver output:
a `separable` case is RE-RANKED with its witness and must come out first; an `in-hull` case is REBUILT from its
combination and must reach `1e-9`. Certificates that fail fall through to `undecided`.

### The two bases, which are the point

| Basis   | What a direction may move                               |  hits | separable | in-hull | undecided |           ceiling |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----: | --------: | ------: | --------: | ----------------: |
| `slope` | any of the 14 terms, including the ones shipped at zero | 1 073 |       349 |       0 |         0 | **1 422 (100 %)** |
| `paid`  | only the terms that already pay (`weight × slope`)      | 1 073 |       217 | **131** |         1 |   1 290 (90.72 %) |

**The support is the constraint, not the values.** With the support frozen, 131 misses are provably unreachable — no
re-weighting of the paying terms separates them, because on those columns their answers are convex combinations of
their competitors. With the support open, **all 349** are reachable, each by a vector of its own, and that is the
answer to the sentence 274 wrote. The `slope` reading also states its own limit honestly: in 14 dimensions with ~49
candidates a point is almost always a vertex, so `in-hull = 0` there is a fact about dimensionality and not about
headroom. The theorem earns its place in the frozen-support space, where it _decides_ 131 cases.

### The positive result: one vector transfers

`heldOutFit` fits a ranking perceptron on the alternating even cases, reads it on the odd ones, and swaps — three seeds
by two orientations, because one fit is an anecdote.

| Fit                  |  recorded |     start |  fitted |                 vs recorded |
| -------------------- | --------: | --------: | ------: | --------------------------: |
| train (711)          |       542 |       518 |     605 |                     **+63** |
| held (711)           |       531 |       513 |     580 |                     **+49** |
| held, five more fits | 531 / 542 | 513 / 518 | 576–594 | **+45, +51, +52, +38, +49** |

**Six of six held-out halves improve, `+38` to `+52`, mean `+47.3` (`+6.7 pp`), with no engine change, no new term and
no model call.** The training half rises further (`85.1 %` against the held half's `81.6 %`), and the 25-case gap
between them is the overfit the design exists to expose rather than to hide.

### And it does not ship, because the family gate refuses it

Net `+112` (`1 185` against `1 073`), gross `+131`, and `+84` of the gross sits in two `HTTP…Replace…` families —
while **three families above the 20-case floor lose cases**: `HTTPRequestAbort −3`, `HTTPRequestReplacePath −4`,
`NetworkDelay −6`. The pre-registered rule _no family with `n ≥ 20` may lose a case the shipped run answered_ rejects
it. Same bar that killed `prism 0.02` at 274, applied to a result twenty times larger; a gate applied only to small
numbers is not a gate. The next subject is the **constrained** fit — maximise the count subject to the family floor,
which is LP-shaped rather than perceptron-shaped.

### The defect found on the way: the shipped run is not one weight vector

The fit starts where the dump says the formula started, and there it scores `518` of the training half against the
`542` the dump RECORDED. A 24-case gap at `Δw = 0` is not a fitting artefact. The census names the term:

| `failedEdge` weight in the dump | Cases |
| ------------------------------- | ----: |
| `0`                             | 1 114 |
| absent (never fired)            |   200 |
| `3`                             |   108 |

One corpus, one dispatch family, **two different values for the same weight**. "The shipped configuration" — the
baseline every ablation in this repository subtracts from — is a mixture of two configurations, and no single vector
reproduces it. Recorded as an open defect with its measurement; the repair changes every published baseline and needs
the two batches traced first.

### What this changes

The next step is no longer "a term with a different shape". It is (1) the constrained fit, which the unconstrained one
already proves is worth most of `+6.7 pp`, and (2) the per-case **selection**, because the per-case ceiling is `100 %`
and one vector reaches `81.6 %` — that distance is the agent layer's quantified target, with the parameter switch the
project requires. The 131 frozen-support cases are a separate line: they need a term TURNED ON, and six terms ship at
zero on this corpus.
